42852.q: In which year did the August Coup take place in Moscow?
42852.e: The coup lasted from 19 to 21 August 1991. Communist hardliners wanted to stop the reforms.
42852.m: The August Coup took place in 1991.

42853.q: Who did the coup leaders want to remove from power in August 1991?
42853.e: The coup leaders wanted to depose Gorbachev and prevent a new Union Treaty. This would have given the republics more rights.
42853.m: The August Coup was aimed at Gorbachev.

42854.q: Where was Gorbachev held during the August Coup?
a: At his holiday home in Crimea
42854.e: Gorbachev was on holiday in Foros on the Crimean peninsula. The coup leaders cut him off from the outside world there.
42854.m: During the coup Gorbachev was stuck in Crimea.

42855.q: Which ballet did Soviet television show again and again during the coup?
42855.e: Instead of news, television showed Tchaikovsky’s “Swan Lake” for hours. The ballet became a symbol of the coup.
42855.m: During the August Coup “Swan Lake” was on television.

42856.q: How long did the August Coup last before it failed?
42856.e: The coup began on 19 August and collapsed on 21 August 1991. Soldiers refused to shoot at the people.
42856.m: The August Coup failed after three days.

42857.q: What did the coup leaders in Moscow declare in August 1991?
42857.e: Eight senior officials, including the head of the KGB, called themselves the State Committee on the State of Emergency. In this way they wanted to seize power.
42857.m: The coup leaders declared a state of emergency in 1991.

42858.q: What was the result of the failure of the August Coup?
a: The break-up of the Soviet Union speeded up
Gorbachev became more powerful than ever
42858.e: After the coup many Soviet republics declared independence, and the Communist Party lost its power. By the end of 1991 the Soviet Union no longer existed.
42858.m: The failed coup speeded up the end of the Soviet Union.

42859.q: Where was Boris Yeltsin standing on 19 August 1991 when he gave a famous speech?
42859.e: In front of the White House in Moscow, Yeltsin climbed onto a tank and called for resistance. The picture went around the world.
42859.m: In 1991 Yeltsin called for resistance from a tank.

42860.q: Which office did Boris Yeltsin take up in July 1991 as Russia’s first politician elected by the people?
42860.e: On 12 June 1991 Yeltsin won Russia’s first free presidential election. He took office in July 1991.
42860.m: Yeltsin was Russia’s first freely elected president.

42861.q: Which party did Boris Yeltsin publicly leave in July 1990?
a: Communist Party of the Soviet Union
42861.e: At the 1990 Party Congress, Yeltsin announced that he was leaving the CPSU. In doing so he clearly opposed the old Party leadership.
42861.m: Yeltsin left the Communist Party in 1990.

42862.q: Until which year was Boris Yeltsin President of Russia?
42862.e: Yeltsin surprisingly resigned on 31 December 1999. His health was poor.
42862.m: Yeltsin resigned at the end of 1999.

42863.q: Who followed Boris Yeltsin as President of Russia?
42863.e: At the end of 1999 Yeltsin handed over his duties to his prime minister. He was also elected President in March 2000.

42864.q: Which building did Yeltsin have shelled in October 1993 during a dispute with Parliament?
42864.e: In the constitutional crisis of 1993, Yeltsin had tanks fire on the parliament building. After that he pushed through a new constitution with a strong president.
42864.m: In 1993 Yeltsin had the Russian parliament building shelled.

42865.q: In which country was Boris Yeltsin President?
42865.e: Boris Yeltsin was President of Russia from 1991 to 1999. He was the country’s first freely elected president.
42865.m: Boris Yeltsin was President of Russia.

42866.q: What is the CIS, which was founded at the end of 1991?
a: An association of former Soviet republics
42866.e: CIS stands for Commonwealth of Independent States. After the end of the Soviet Union many former Soviet republics joined together in it.
42866.m: In the CIS former Soviet republics work together.

42867.q: Which three republics first founded the CIS?
42867.e: The three Slavic republics signed the founding agreement. Two weeks later more republics joined.
42867.m: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus founded the CIS.

42868.q: Which state was no longer on the map at the end of 1991?
42868.e: On 25 December 1991 Gorbachev resigned as President. The next day the Soviet Union was officially dissolved.
42868.m: The Soviet Union was dissolved at the end of 1991.

42869.q: Which country left the CIS in 2009 after a war with Russia?
42869.e: After the war over South Ossetia in August 2008, Georgia announced it was leaving. This took effect in August 2009.

42870.q: In which city is the CIS based?
42870.e: The CIS Executive Committee is based in Minsk, the capital of Belarus. The founding agreement was also drawn up there in 1991.
42870.m: The CIS is based in Minsk.

42871.q: Which former Soviet republics never joined the CIS?
42871.e: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania saw themselves as occupied countries, not as part of the Soviet Union. They aimed to join the EU and NATO.
42871.m: The Baltic states were never members of the CIS.

42872.q: Which two states are meant by “Two” in the Two Plus Four Treaty?
42872.e: The two German states negotiated together with the four victorious powers of the Second World War. It was about the conditions for German unity.
42872.m: The “Two” in the treaty are the two German states.

42873.q: Which countries are meant by “Four” in the Two Plus Four Treaty?
a: USA, Soviet Union, Great Britain and France
42873.e: The four victorious powers of the Second World War still had rights in Germany and Berlin. With the treaty they gave them up.
42873.m: The “Four” are the victorious powers of the Second World War.

42874.q: In which city was the Two Plus Four Treaty signed?
42874.e: The foreign ministers of the six states signed the treaty in the Soviet capital. It cleared the way for German unity.
42874.m: The Two Plus Four Treaty was signed in Moscow.

42875.q: When was the Two Plus Four Treaty signed?
42875.e: The signing took place on 12 September 1990. A few weeks later the two German states were united.
42875.m: The Two Plus Four Treaty dates from September 1990.

42876.q: Which event did the Two Plus Four Treaty make possible?
a: The building of the Berlin Wall
42876.e: The treaty settled the external questions of German unity. On 3 October 1990 East Germany joined the Federal Republic.
42876.m: The Two Plus Four Treaty made German unity possible.

42877.q: Which border was confirmed as final in the Two Plus Four Treaty?
42877.e: Germany confirmed that the border along the Oder and Neisse rivers is final. In doing so it gave up former eastern territories.
42877.m: The Oder-Neisse border was finally recognised in 1990.

42878.q: According to the Two Plus Four Treaty, which weapons did united Germany have to give up?
42878.e: Germany gave up nuclear, biological and chemical weapons. It also had to reduce the size of its army.
42878.m: United Germany gave up nuclear weapons.

42879.q: Which foreign troops had to leave Germany after the Two Plus Four Treaty?
42879.e: Soviet soldiers had been in eastern Germany since 1945. According to the treaty they had to withdraw; the last ones left in 1994.
42879.m: The Soviet troops withdrew from Germany after unification.

42880.q: Roughly how long did the Long March last?
42880.e: The Long March began in October 1934 and ended in October 1935. So the soldiers were on the move for about a year.
42880.m: The Long March lasted about a year.

42881.q: Why did the Chinese Communists set off on the Long March in 1934?
a: They were fleeing their enemies in the civil war
They wanted to go on a pilgrimage
They were holding a sports competition
42881.e: The Nationalist army had encircled the Communists in southern China. To avoid defeat they broke out and moved far away.
42881.m: On the Long March the Communists fled from their enemies.

42882.q: How did most soldiers cover the Long March?
42882.e: The soldiers marched thousands of kilometres on foot. They crossed mountains, rivers and swamps.
42882.m: The Long March was made on foot.

42883.q: To which part of China did the Communists move on the Long March?
42883.e: The Communists moved from the south to the north of China. There the march ended in 1935 in Shaanxi province.
42883.m: The Long March led to the north of China.

42884.q: Who became the most important leader of the Chinese Communists during the Long March?
42884.e: During the Long March Mao Zedong gradually took over the leadership. Later he founded the People’s Republic of China.
42884.m: On the Long March Mao became the leader.

42885.q: How many of the soldiers who set off on the Long March reached the end?
42885.e: Of over 85,000 people who set off, only about 7,000 reached the end. Many died in fighting or from hunger, cold or disease.
42885.m: Only a small part of the soldiers survived the Long March.

42886.q: What role does the Long March play in the Chinese Communist Party’s version of history today?
a: It is seen as the Party’s heroic epic
It is seen as a defeat
It is seen as the enemy’s work
42886.e: The Party celebrates the march as proof of courage and determination. It is an important founding myth of the People’s Republic.
42886.m: The Long March is a founding myth of the Chinese Communist Party.

42887.q: What did the soldiers on the Long March have to get across?
a: The ice at the North Pole
42887.e: The route led over snow-covered mountains, through swamps and across wild rivers. Many soldiers died on the way.
42887.m: The Long March led through mountains and across rivers.

42889.q: Whose large portrait still hangs on the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, where the People’s Republic of China was proclaimed?
42889.e: In 1949 Mao proclaimed the People’s Republic of China on this gate. His portrait still hangs there today and is a symbol of the state.
42889.m: A portrait of Mao Zedong hangs on the Gate of Heavenly Peace.

42890.q: Where did the Kuomintang government flee after its defeat in the civil war in 1949?
42890.e: Chiang Kai-shek withdrew with his government and army to the island of Taiwan. The Republic of China still exists there today.
42890.m: After 1949 the Kuomintang continued to govern on the island of Taiwan.

42891.q: Which party has governed the People’s Republic of China since it was founded in 1949?
42891.e: Since 1949 the Communist Party has ruled China alone. Other parties have no real power.
42891.m: The Communist Party has ruled China since 1949.

42892.q: Which city became the capital of the People’s Republic of China in 1949, after Nanjing had been the seat of government before?
42892.e: The Kuomintang had governed from Nanjing. In 1949 the Communists made Beijing the capital again.
42892.m: Beijing has been China’s capital since 1949.

42893.q: What does the big star on the flag of the People’s Republic of China symbolise?
42893.e: The big star stands for leadership by the Communist Party. The four small stars stand for the social classes of the people.
42893.m: The big star on China’s flag stands for the Communist Party.

42894.q: With which country did the young People’s Republic of China sign a friendship treaty in 1950?
42894.e: In February 1950 Mao and Stalin signed a treaty of friendship and alliance in Moscow. The Soviet Union then helped China with loans and experts.
42894.m: At first the Soviet Union was the People’s Republic of China’s most important partner.

42895.q: What is the real title of the so-called Mao Bible?
42895.e: The book was officially called “Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung”. Because of its red cover it is also called “The Little Red Book”.
42895.m: The Mao Bible is really called “Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung”.

42896.q: What is in the Mao Bible?
a: Poems from the time of the emperors
42896.e: The Mao Bible is a collection of short quotations from speeches and writings by Mao Zedong. They are arranged by topic.
42896.m: The Mao Bible is a collection of quotations.

42897.q: Who was the Mao Bible first printed for?
a: For the soldiers of the Chinese army
42897.e: The collection of quotations was first made for training soldiers. Only later was it handed out to the whole population.
42897.m: The Mao Bible was first made for the soldiers.

42898.q: At what time was the Mao Bible especially important in China?
a: In the time of the emperors
42898.e: The Mao Bible appeared in 1964. In the Cultural Revolution from 1966, almost everyone had to own a copy and learn from it.
42898.m: In the Cultural Revolution the Mao Bible was everywhere.

42899.q: How important is the Mao Bible in China today compared with the Cultural Revolution?
a: Just as important, everyone has to carry it
It is the most important school book
42899.e: After the end of the Cultural Revolution the collection of quotations lost much of its importance. In 1979 the Party even stopped it being printed.
42899.m: Today the Mao Bible is much less important in China.

42901.q: Why is the Mao Bible one of the most printed books in the world?
a: It was handed out in huge numbers in China
It was compulsory reading in Europe
It was sold worldwide as a school book
42901.e: The state had the book printed in enormous numbers and translated into many languages. Estimates range from over one billion to several billion copies.
42901.m: The Mao Bible was printed in enormous numbers.

42902.q: Where outside China was the Mao Bible also popular with some students at the end of the 1960s?
a: In Western countries such as Germany
42902.e: In the student movement around 1968, some young people in Western Europe also carried the book as a political sign. Many knew little at the time about the violence of the Cultural Revolution.
42902.m: Around 1968 the Mao Bible was also known among some students in the West.

42903.q: In which country is the city of Shenzhen?
42903.e: Shenzhen is in the south of China. In 1980 it became one of the country’s first special economic zones.
42903.m: Shenzhen is a big city in China.

42904.q: Which area does Shenzhen directly border?
42904.e: Shenzhen lies just north of Hong Kong. This position was important for attracting money and companies from Hong Kong.
42904.m: Shenzhen lies right on the border with Hong Kong.

42905.q: Which party governed China when the special economic zones were created?
42905.e: China has been governed by the Communist Party since 1949. Under Deng Xiaoping it opened up the economy to foreign companies from 1978.
42905.m: The Communist Party introduced the economic reforms in China.

a: A small town with fishing villages
42906.e: The main town of Bao’an county on the border with Hong Kong had only around 30,000 inhabitants until 1979. Today Shenzhen is one of China’s biggest cities.
42906.m: Shenzhen grew from a small town into a giant city.

42907.q: Roughly how many inhabitants did Shenzhen have according to the 2020 census?
42907.e: In the 2020 census about 17.6 million inhabitants were counted in Shenzhen. That is about twice as many people as live in the whole of Switzerland.
42907.m: More people live in Shenzhen than in the whole of Switzerland.

42908.q: What was different in a special economic zone like Shenzhen compared with the rest of China?
a: Foreign companies were allowed to invest there
Chinese law did not apply there
You were not allowed to work there
Chinese people paid no taxes there
42908.e: In the special economic zones there were tax advantages and freer rules for companies. This was meant to bring foreign money and modern technology into the country.
42908.m: Special economic zones attracted foreign companies to China.

42909.q: In which part of China is Shenzhen?
a: In the south on the coast
In the north in the desert
In the west in the high mountains
In the north-east on the border with Russia
42909.e: Shenzhen lies in the south of China on the Pearl River Delta, right next to Hong Kong. Its position by the sea is good for trade.
42909.m: Shenzhen lies on China’s south coast.

42910.q: How did China’s economy change after the reforms from 1978?
a: It was taken over by Russia
42910.e: Thanks to opening up to foreign companies, China’s economy grew very strongly for decades. Cities like Shenzhen became huge.
42910.m: After the reforms China’s economy grew very quickly.

42911.q: Which country does Xi Jinping govern?
42911.e: Xi Jinping is head of the Chinese Communist Party and President of the state. This makes him the most powerful politician in China.

42912.q: Which party does Xi Jinping lead?
42912.e: In China there is one party that decides everything: the Communist Party. Xi Jinping is its General Secretary.
42912.m: Xi Jinping is head of the Chinese Communist Party.

42913.q: What did China change in 2018 about the President’s term of office?
a: The limit of two terms was removed
The term was shortened to one year
The President is now elected by the people
42913.e: In 2018 the limit of two terms was removed from the constitution. This allowed Xi Jinping to start a third term as President in 2023.
42913.m: Since 2018 the Chinese President’s time in office is no longer limited.

42914.q: What is the big infrastructure project that Xi Jinping announced in 2013 called?
42914.e: The New Silk Road is meant to create trade routes with ports, railways and roads to Asia, Africa and Europe. Its official name is the “Belt and Road Initiative”.
42914.m: The New Silk Road is Xi Jinping’s big trade project.

42915.q: What is the capital of the country that Xi Jinping governs?
42915.e: Beijing is the capital of China. Xi Jinping’s government is based there. Xi Jinping was also born in Beijing.

42916.q: Where did the young Xi Jinping have to live and work for several years during the Cultural Revolution?
a: In a village in the countryside
At a university in the USA
42916.e: Like millions of other young people, Xi was sent to the countryside. From 1969 he lived in a village in Shaanxi province.
42916.m: As a young man Xi Jinping lived in a village in the countryside.

42917.q: What is one of Xi Jinping’s best-known campaigns at home?
42917.e: Since 2012 hundreds of thousands of officials have been punished in the fight against corruption. Critics say that political opponents have also been removed this way.
42917.m: Xi Jinping leads a big campaign against corruption.

42918.q: What does the Party call Xi Jinping’s political ideas, which were written into the constitution?
42918.e: “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era” has been in the Party constitution since 2017 and in the state constitution since 2018. No Party leader since Mao has been honoured like this during his lifetime.
42918.m: Xi Jinping Thought is in China’s constitution.

42919.q: What is the National People’s Congress?
a: The parliament of the People’s Republic of China
42919.e: According to the constitution, the National People’s Congress is the highest organ of state power. In reality, however, the Communist Party decides policy.
42919.m: The National People’s Congress is China’s parliament.

42920.q: Roughly how many members does the National People’s Congress have?
42920.e: The People’s Congress has just under 3,000 members. This makes it one of the biggest parliaments in the world.
42920.m: The National People’s Congress has around 3,000 members.

42921.q: In which building in Beijing does the National People’s Congress meet?
a: In the Great Hall of the People
42921.e: The Great Hall of the People stands on Tiananmen Square. It was completed in 1959.
42921.m: The People’s Congress meets in the Great Hall of the People.

42922.q: How often does the National People’s Congress meet in full session?
42922.e: The full session takes place every year in March and lasts only about a week. Between sessions the Standing Committee does the work.
42922.m: The National People’s Congress meets once a year.

42923.q: Who really decides policy in China, even though the National People’s Congress is the parliament?
42923.e: In China only one party has real power, the Communist Party. The People’s Congress usually approves its plans.
42923.m: In China the Communist Party decides policy.

42924.q: Who officially elects the President in China?
42924.e: According to the constitution, the People’s Congress elects the President. But the Party has already chosen the candidate beforehand.
42924.m: The National People’s Congress elects China’s President.

42925.q: Why is the National People’s Congress often called a “rubber-stamp parliament”?
a: It almost always approves the Party’s proposals
It has no voting rights at all
It is made up only of foreigners
42925.e: Votes usually end with very large majorities for the Party leadership’s proposals. There is no real opposition in the People’s Congress.
42925.m: The National People’s Congress almost always approves the Party’s plans.

42926.q: What is the body called that passes laws between the sessions of the National People’s Congress?
42926.e: The Standing Committee has about 170 members and meets regularly. It does a large part of the law-making.
42926.m: The Standing Committee works between the sessions of the People’s Congress.

42927.q: When was North Korea founded as a separate state?
a: Shortly after the Second World War
42927.e: North Korea was founded in 1948, three years after the end of the Second World War. Kim Il-sung became its first ruler.
42927.m: North Korea was created shortly after the Second World War.

42928.q: Which great power helped Kim Il-sung come to power after the Second World War?
42928.e: After 1945 the Soviet Union occupied the north of Korea. It supported Kim Il-sung as leader of the new state.
42928.m: Kim Il-sung came to power with the help of the Soviet Union.

42929.q: Which war did Kim Il-sung start in 1950 with an attack on the South?
42929.e: In June 1950 North Korea attacked South Korea. The war ended in 1953 with a ceasefire but without a peace treaty.
42929.m: Kim Il-sung started the Korean War in 1950.

42930.q: How long did Kim Il-sung rule North Korea?
42930.e: Kim Il-sung ruled from the founding in 1948 until his death in 1994. There are no free elections in North Korea.
42930.m: Kim Il-sung ruled North Korea until his death.

42931.q: Who followed Kim Il-sung as ruler of North Korea?
42931.e: After Kim Il-sung’s death, his son Kim Jong-il took power. Today his grandson, Kim Jong-un, is already in charge.
42931.m: Kim Il-sung founded a family dynasty in North Korea.

42932.q: What title did Kim Il-sung receive in North Korea’s constitution after his death?
42932.e: In 1998 Kim Il-sung was declared “Eternal President” in the constitution. This was meant to keep him at the head of the state for ever.
42932.m: In North Korea Kim Il-sung is regarded as the “Eternal President”.

42933.q: Which day is a big holiday in North Korea, known as the “Day of the Sun”?
42933.e: Kim Il-sung was born on 15 April 1912. His birthday is celebrated every year in North Korea with big festivities.
42933.m: In North Korea Kim Il-sung’s birthday is celebrated as the “Day of the Sun”.

42934.q: What is the exaggerated worship of Kim Il-sung in North Korea called?
42934.e: All over the country there are statues and pictures of Kim Il-sung. People have to bow in front of his monuments.
42934.m: There is a strong personality cult around Kim Il-sung.

42935.q: Roughly what does the Korean word “Juche” mean?
42935.e: Juche means something like “self-reliance” or “independence”. According to this idea, a country should provide for itself politically, economically and militarily.

42936.q: In which country is the Juche ideology the official state ideology?
42936.e: The Juche ideology is written into North Korea’s constitution. It shapes politics, school and art there.
42936.m: The Juche ideology is North Korea’s state idea.

42937.q: Who is regarded as the founder of the Juche ideology?
42937.e: Kim Il-sung put the Juche idea in the foreground from the 1950s. His successors later developed it further.
42937.m: Kim Il-sung founded the Juche ideology.

42938.q: Roughly how tall is the Juche Tower in Pyongyang?
42938.e: The Juche Tower was opened in 1982 for the 70th birthday of the state’s founder. Including the flame at the top, it is about 170 metres tall.
42938.m: The Juche Tower in Pyongyang is about 170 metres tall.

42939.q: With which year does the Juche calendar in North Korea start counting?
a: The year North Korea was founded
The end of the Korean War
42939.e: 1912, the year Kim Il-sung was born, is year 1 in the Juche calendar. The calendar was introduced in 1997.
42939.m: The Juche calendar starts with Kim Il-sung’s year of birth, 1912.

42940.q: What economic effect did the Juche policy of isolation have on North Korea?
a: The country stayed poor and isolated
The country became Asia’s biggest exporter
The country became a magnet for tourists
42940.e: North Korea trades very little with other countries and has hardly any contact with the outside world. In the 1990s the country suffered a severe famine.
42940.m: Isolation has made North Korea poor and cut off.

42941.q: What was given priority in North Korea under the Songun policy from the 1990s?
42941.e: Songun means “military first”. The army got the most money and resources, while many people went hungry.
42941.m: In North Korea Songun means “military first”.

42942.q: According to the Juche ideology, what should people in North Korea mainly follow?
42942.e: According to the Juche ideology, the people need a great leader to guide them. In this way it justifies the power of the Kim family.
42942.m: The Juche ideology justifies the power of the Kim family.

42943.q: Which country carried out the reforms called “Doi Moi”?
42943.e: The Communist Party of Vietnam decided on Doi Moi in 1986. The country’s economy was in a serious crisis at the time.
42943.m: Doi Moi were economic reforms in Vietnam.

42944.q: What does the Vietnamese term “Doi Moi” mean?
42944.e: Doi Moi translates as “renewal”. It refers to the restructuring of the economy.

42945.q: What mainly changed in Vietnam because of Doi Moi?
a: The economy opened up to the market
42945.e: Farmers and businesses were again allowed to make more of their own decisions and to make profits. Politically, however, the Communist Party stayed alone in power.
42945.m: Doi Moi opened up Vietnam’s economy, but the Party stayed in power.

42946.q: Which country served Vietnam as a model for the Doi Moi reforms?
42946.e: China had been successful with market reforms since 1978. Vietnam followed a similar path.
42946.m: For Doi Moi, Vietnam followed China’s example.

42947.q: How did things change for Vietnam with rice after the Doi Moi reforms?
a: It became one of the biggest rice exporters
It had to import even more rice
It gave up growing rice completely
It was no longer allowed to sell rice
42947.e: Before the reforms, Vietnam had to import rice. A few years later it was one of the world’s biggest rice exporters.
42947.m: After Doi Moi Vietnam became a big rice exporter.

42948.q: With which former enemy in war did Vietnam restore diplomatic relations in 1995?
42948.e: In the Vietnam War the USA had fought against North Vietnam. In 1995 the two countries normalised their relations, which brought Vietnam more trade.
42948.m: Vietnam and the USA have had diplomatic relations again since 1995.

42949.q: Which international trade organisation did Vietnam join in 2007?
42949.e: Joining the WTO was an important step in opening up. It made it easier for Vietnam to export all over the world.
42949.m: Vietnam has been a member of the WTO since 2007.

42950.q: What happened to poverty in Vietnam in the decades after Doi Moi?
42950.e: The economy grew quickly for many years. The share of very poor people fell considerably.
42950.m: After Doi Moi poverty in Vietnam fell sharply.

42951.q: What happened in Cuba on New Year’s Day 1959?
a: The dictator fled and the revolutionaries won
Cuba became part of the USA
42951.e: On New Year’s Eve 1959 the dictator left the country. This meant Fidel Castro and his fighters had won.
42951.m: The Cuban Revolution triumphed on 1 January 1959.

42952.q: Who did the Cuban revolutionaries overthrow?
42952.e: The dictator Fulgencio Batista ruled Cuba harshly and unjustly. The revolutionaries led by Fidel Castro drove him out.
42952.m: The Cuban Revolution overthrew a dictator.

42953.q: What are fighters called who, like Castro’s rebels, fight an army in small groups from mountains and forests?
42953.e: Guerrilla means “little war” in Spanish. Castro’s rebels attacked the army and then withdrew to the mountains again.
42953.m: Castro’s rebels fought a guerrilla war.

42954.q: How did Fidel Castro and his fighters get from Mexico to Cuba in 1956?
42954.e: 82 fighters crossed the sea to Cuba on the small yacht “Granma”. The journey was very cramped and dangerous.
42954.m: Castro’s fighters came to Cuba on a small boat.

42955.q: Where did Castro’s rebels hide from 1956?
a: In the mountains in the east of Cuba
In the presidential palace in Havana
In a city in the USA
42955.e: The rebels withdrew into the Sierra Maestra mountains. There they were hard to find and built up their army.
42955.m: The Cuban rebels hid in the mountains.

42956.q: How did the USA respond economically to the confiscations in Cuba from 1960?
42956.e: The new government also nationalised companies from the USA. In response the USA imposed an embargo that is still largely in force today.
42956.m: The USA imposed a trade embargo on Cuba.

42957.q: How did the Cuban Revolution end?
42957.e: At the end of 1958 the rebels won the decisive battles. At the beginning of 1959 Fidel Castro took power.
42957.m: The Cuban Revolution ended with the rebels’ victory.

42958.q: Which country became Cuba’s most important ally after the revolution?
42958.e: Cuba bought oil from the Soviet Union and sold it sugar. After the end of the Soviet Union in 1991, Cuba fell into a severe economic crisis.
42958.m: After the revolution the Soviet Union was Cuba’s most important partner.

42959.q: How was Raúl Castro related to Fidel Castro?
42959.e: Raúl Castro was born in 1931 and was five years younger than Fidel. Both fought together in the revolution.
42959.m: Raúl Castro is Fidel Castro’s younger brother.

42960.q: Which office did Raúl Castro hold for almost 50 years before he became President?
42960.e: Raúl Castro was Minister of Defence from 1959 to 2008. He built up the Cuban army.
42960.m: Raúl Castro was Cuba’s Minister of Defence for decades.

42961.q: Why did Raúl Castro temporarily take over Fidel’s duties in 2006?
42961.e: Fidel Castro had to have an operation in 2006. Raúl then ran things and officially became President in 2008.
42961.m: Raúl Castro took over the leadership in 2006 because Fidel was ill.

42962.q: Until which year was Raúl Castro President of Cuba?
42962.e: In 2018 Raúl Castro gave up the presidency. For the first time since 1976, no Castro was head of state.
42962.m: Raúl Castro was President of Cuba until 2018.

42963.q: Who followed Raúl Castro as President of Cuba in 2018?
42963.e: Miguel Díaz-Canel was born in 1960, so only after the revolution. Before that he was First Vice-President of Cuba.
42963.m: Miguel Díaz-Canel followed Raúl Castro in 2018.

42964.q: With which US president did Raúl Castro improve relations with the USA?
42964.e: At the end of 2014 both announced a rapprochement. In 2015 embassies opened again, and in 2016 Obama visited Havana.
42964.m: Raúl Castro and Barack Obama improved relations between Cuba and the USA.

42965.q: What did Raúl Castro increasingly allow Cubans to have from 2010?
a: A separate currency for each province
42965.e: Under Raúl Castro more people were allowed to work for themselves, for example with small restaurants or taxis. One-party rule remained.
42965.m: Raúl Castro allowed more small private businesses in Cuba.

42966.q: From which year did the one-child policy apply in China?
42966.e: The rules were announced in 1979 and enforced across the country from 1980. They were meant to slow down the fast growth of the population.
42966.m: The one-child policy applied in China from 1980.

42967.q: What was the main aim of the one-child policy?
a: To get more children into school
42967.e: At the end of the 1970s China had almost a billion inhabitants. The government feared that there would not be enough food and work for everyone.
42967.m: The one-child policy was meant to slow down population growth.

42968.q: From which year were all couples in China allowed to have two children?
42968.e: At the end of 2015 China decided on the two-child policy, which applied from January 2016. The population was getting older and there was a shortage of young workers.
42968.m: Since 2016 all couples in China have been allowed two children.

42969.q: How many children has China allowed each couple since 2021?
42969.e: In 2021 the limit was raised to three children. Later the penalties for having more children were abolished completely.
42969.m: Since 2021 China has allowed three children per couple.

42970.q: What effect did the one-child policy have on the balance of boys and girls in China?
a: There are clearly more men than women
There are clearly more women than men
There are exactly the same number
42970.e: Many families wanted a son. That is why fewer girls were born, and today there are millions of women missing.
42970.m: Because of the one-child policy there are more men than women in China.

42971.q: Which group was usually exempt from the one-child policy?
42971.e: Many of the 55 recognised minorities were allowed to have more children. Farming families also often got a second child if the first was a girl.
42971.m: National minorities were often exempt from the one-child policy.

42972.q: Which problem did the one-child policy make worse in the long run?
a: The number of people who cannot read
42972.e: Because fewer children were born, there are now many older people and fewer young ones. Since 2022 China’s population has been shrinking.
42972.m: The one-child policy made China’s population age faster.

42973.q: How were families punished who broke the one-child policy?
42973.e: Anyone who had too many children often had to pay heavy fines and could even lose their job. The state put great pressure on families.
42973.m: Breaking the one-child policy was punished with heavy fines.

42974.q: Which doctor from Argentina became a comandante in the Cuban Revolution and later Cuba’s Minister of Industry?
42974.e: Che Guevara had studied medicine in Buenos Aires. After the victory he ran the National Bank and the Ministry of Industry, among other things.
42974.m: Che Guevara was a doctor and became a minister in Cuba.

42975.q: What is Shenzhen known for around the world today?
42975.e: A great many mobile phones, computer parts and drones are developed and built in Shenzhen. That is why the city is often called “China’s Silicon Valley”.
42975.m: Shenzhen is a centre for electronics and technology.

42976.q: What were spoilt only children in China called informally?
42976.e: Because parents and four grandparents looked after a single child, people spoke of “little emperors”. The expression describes spoilt only children.
42976.m: In China spoilt only children were called “little emperors”.

42977.q: Where does Kim Il-sung’s embalmed body lie today?
42977.e: His former palace in the capital Pyongyang was converted into a mausoleum. His son Kim Jong-il also lies there.
42977.m: Kim Il-sung lies in a mausoleum in Pyongyang.

42978.e: In Cuba only the Communist Party is allowed. Raúl Castro led it until 2021.
42978.m: Cuba is governed by the Communist Party.

43973.q: Which large forest in Germany is close to Basel?
43973.e: The Black Forest is a range of low mountains in south-west Germany. Its southern part reaches close to Basel.
43973.m: The Black Forest is just north of Basel in Germany.

43974.q: Which famous collectors of fairy tales come from Germany?
43974.e: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected fairy tales such as “Hansel and Gretel” and “Little Red Riding Hood”. They lived in Germany.
43974.m: The Brothers Grimm collected many well-known fairy tales.

43975.q: What is the highest mountain in Germany called?
43975.e: The Zugspitze is about 2,962 metres high. It is in Bavaria on the border with Austria.
43975.m: The Zugspitze is Germany’s highest mountain.

43976.q: Which long loaf of bread is typical of France?
43976.e: The baguette is a long, thin white loaf with a crispy crust. In France people often buy it fresh every day.
43976.m: The baguette is a typically French bread.

43977.q: Which large lake does Switzerland share with France?
43977.e: The northern shore of Lake Geneva belongs to Switzerland, and most of the southern shore belongs to France. In French it is called “Lac Léman”.
43977.m: Lake Geneva lies between Switzerland and France.

43978.q: Which famous food comes from Italy?
43978.e: Pizza comes from Italy, especially from the area around Naples. Today people eat it all over the world.

43979.q: Which city in Italy has canals instead of streets and gondolas as boats?
43979.e: Venice is built on lots of small islands. Instead of cars, boats and gondolas travel along the canals.
43979.m: In Venice you travel by boat instead of by car.

43980.q: In which Italian city does the famous Leaning Tower stand?
43980.e: The Tower of Pisa is a bell tower. Because the ground is soft, it leans.
43980.m: The Leaning Tower stands in Pisa.

43981.q: Which Italian village on Lake Lugano is completely surrounded by Switzerland?
43981.e: Campione d'Italia belongs to Italy but lies in the middle of Ticino. Gandria, Morcote and Brissago are villages in Ticino.
43981.m: Campione d'Italia is an Italian village inside Switzerland.

43982.q: What is the name of the big volcano on the Italian island of Sicily?
43982.e: Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe. It is on Sicily and erupts again and again.
43982.m: Etna is a volcano on Sicily.

43983.q: Which famous chocolate cake comes from Austria?
43983.e: The Sachertorte is a chocolate cake with apricot jam. It was invented by Franz Sacher in 1832.
43983.m: The Sachertorte is a cake from Austria.

43984.q: What is the highest mountain in Austria called?
43984.e: The Grossglockner is about 3798 metres high. It is the highest mountain in Austria.
43984.m: The Grossglockner is Austria's highest mountain.

43985.e: The Grisons borders Austria in the east. The canton of St Gallen also has a border with Austria.
43985.m: The Grisons is a neighbour of Austria.

43986.q: Which animals show off their tricks at the Spanish Riding School in Austria?
43986.e: At the Spanish Riding School, white horses called Lipizzaners perform difficult jumps and steps.
43986.m: At the Spanish Riding School, horses dance.

43987.q: How many federal states does Austria have?
43987.e: Austria is divided into 9 federal states, for example Tyrol, Salzburg and Vorarlberg.

43988.q: Roughly how many people live in Liechtenstein?
43988.e: About 40,000 people live in Liechtenstein (as of 2024). That is fewer than in the city of Lucerne.

43989.q: Which two Swiss cantons does Liechtenstein border?
43989.e: In the west Liechtenstein borders the canton of St Gallen, and in the south the canton of the Grisons.
43989.m: Liechtenstein borders St Gallen and the Grisons.

43990.q: Which of Switzerland's neighbouring countries is the smallest?
43990.e: Liechtenstein covers only about 160 square kilometres. It is one of the smallest countries in the world.

43991.q: What is the name of the Swiss office responsible for customs?
a: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security
43991.e: Since 2022 the Swiss customs authority has been called the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security, or FOCBS (BAZG in German).
43991.m: In Switzerland the FOCBS looks after customs.

43992.q: Which village in the Grisons is duty-free?
43992.e: Samnaun lies outside the Swiss customs area. There you can buy many goods without paying duty.
43992.m: In Samnaun you do not have to pay customs duty.

43993.q: What do you call it when someone secretly takes goods across the border?
43993.e: Anyone who takes goods across the border secretly and without declaring them is smuggling. This is against the law and is punished.

43994.q: Who checks at the border what you bring back from abroad?
43994.e: Customs officers work at the border. They check which goods you bring with you and sometimes ask for money for them.
43994.m: At the border, customs checks the goods.

43995.q: In which city do the Swiss government and parliament work?
43995.e: Bern is called the federal city. The Federal Council and parliament meet in the Federal Palace.
43995.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

43996.q: How do you say ‘Good day’ in French?
43996.e: “Bonjour” means “good day”. “Buongiorno” is Italian, “Hello” is English and “Hola” is Spanish.

43997.q: How do you say ‘Thank you’ in Italian?
43997.e: “Grazie” means “thank you”. “Prego” means “you're welcome” and “Ciao” means “hello” or “bye”.

44000.q: Which national language of Switzerland is spoken almost only in the canton of the Grisons?
44000.e: Romansh is spoken mainly in the Grisons, for example in the Engadine. It is the smallest of the four national languages.
44000.m: Romansh is spoken mainly in the Grisons.

44001.q: Which flying machine used to be built in Friedrichshafen on Lake Constance?
44001.e: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin built large airships on Lake Constance. The first Zeppelin rose above the lake in 1900.
44001.m: The Zeppelin comes from Lake Constance.

44002.q: What is the highest mountain in the Alps, on the border between France and Italy, called?
44002.e: Mont Blanc is about 4800 metres high. It lies on the border between France and Italy.
44002.m: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps.

44003.q: What is the famous cycle race that goes through France every summer called?
44003.e: The Tour de France has existed since 1903. The riders are on the road for about three weeks.
44003.m: The Tour de France is the most famous cycle race in the world.

44004.q: Which warm sea does France border in the south?
44004.e: In the south France lies on the Mediterranean, for example at Marseille and Nice. In the west it borders the Atlantic.
44004.m: France lies on the Mediterranean in the south.

44005.q: Which purple flowers bloom in huge fields in Provence in summer?
44005.e: Provence is in the south of France. Huge lavender fields grow there and smell very strongly.
44005.m: Lavender blooms in Provence in summer.

44006.q: Which enormous palace did King Louis XIV have built in France?
44006.e: The Palace of Versailles is near Paris. It has a famous Hall of Mirrors and a huge park.
44006.m: Louis XIV had the Palace of Versailles built.

44007.q: Which animal is a well-known symbol of France?
44007.e: The Gallic cockerel is an old symbol of France. You often see it on sports teams.
44007.m: The cockerel is a symbol of France.

44008.q: Which soft cheese comes from France?
44008.e: Camembert comes from Normandy in the north of France. It is soft inside and has a white rind.
44008.m: Camembert is a cheese from France.

44009.q: Which German city has the biggest port in the country?
44009.e: Hamburg lies on the river Elbe, not far from the North Sea. Huge container ships dock there.
44009.m: Hamburg has the biggest port in Germany.

44010.q: In which German city on the Rhine is there a famous cathedral with two tall towers?
44010.e: Cologne Cathedral is over 150 metres high. People worked on building it for over 600 years.
44010.m: Cologne Cathedral stands on the Rhine.

44011.q: In which German city does the Oktoberfest take place every year?
44011.e: The Oktoberfest in Munich is the biggest folk festival in the world. It already starts in September.
44011.m: The Oktoberfest takes place in Munich.

44012.q: Which two seas does Germany border?
a: The North Sea and the Baltic Sea
The Mediterranean and the North Sea
The Baltic Sea and the Mediterranean
The Black Sea and the Baltic Sea
44012.e: In the north Germany lies on the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. There are lots of islands and beaches there.
44012.m: Germany lies on the North Sea and the Baltic Sea.

44013.q: Which fairy-tale castle stands in Bavaria?
44013.e: King Ludwig II had Neuschwanstein Castle built. It looks like a castle from a fairy tale.
44013.m: Neuschwanstein is a fairy-tale castle in Bavaria.

44014.q: How many neighbouring countries does Germany have?
44014.e: Germany borders nine countries, for example Switzerland, France, Poland and Denmark.

44015.q: Which large island in the Mediterranean belongs to Italy?
44015.e: Sardinia lies west of the Italian mainland and belongs to Italy. Corsica belongs to France.

44016.q: Which big Italian city lies not far from Ticino and is known for fashion?
44016.e: Milan is in Lombardy, about an hour's drive from Lugano. The city is famous for fashion and its cathedral.
44016.m: Milan is a big fashion city near Switzerland.

44017.q: What is the longest river in Italy called?
44017.e: The Po flows through northern Italy to the Adriatic Sea. It is the longest river in the country.
44017.m: The Po is the longest river in Italy.

44018.q: Which neighbouring country lies to the south of Switzerland?
44018.e: South of the Alps, Valais, Ticino and the Grisons border Italy.
44018.m: Italy lies to the south of Switzerland.

44019.q: Which breaded meat dish is typical of Austria?
44019.e: Wiener Schnitzel is a thin, breaded veal escalope. It is a national dish of Austria.
44019.m: Wiener Schnitzel is a typical dish from Austria.

44020.e: Austria lies in the middle of Europe and has no coast. Just like Switzerland, it is a landlocked country.

44021.q: Which city in Tyrol has hosted the Winter Olympics twice?
44021.e: Innsbruck hosted the Winter Olympics in 1964 and 1976. The city lies right in the middle of the Alps.
44021.m: Innsbruck has hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

44022.q: Which river flows from the Engadine to Austria?
44022.e: The Inn rises in the Engadine in the Grisons. It flows through Tyrol and later joins the Danube.
44022.m: The Inn flows from the Engadine to Austria.

44024.q: What has Liechtenstein not had since 1868?
44024.e: Liechtenstein abolished its army in 1868. Since then the country has had no soldiers.

44025.q: What is the well-known ski resort in Liechtenstein called?
44025.e: Malbun lies in the mountains of the municipality of Triesenberg. It is the only big ski resort in Liechtenstein.

44026.q: What is Liechtenstein famous for among collectors?
44026.e: For over 100 years Liechtenstein has issued its own beautifully designed stamps. There is even a postal museum in Vaduz.
44026.m: Liechtenstein is known for its stamps.

44027.e: Liechtenstein is too small for its own airport. People who want to fly usually travel to Zurich.
44027.m: Liechtenstein has no airport of its own.

44028.q: Which border town in Ticino lies at the very south of Switzerland?
44028.e: Chiasso lies right on the border with Italy. The southernmost point of Switzerland is near Chiasso.
44028.m: Chiasso lies at the very south of Switzerland.

44029.q: Where does the border run in Lake Geneva?
a: Through the middle of the lake
44029.e: The border between Switzerland and France runs through the water in the middle of Lake Geneva.
44029.m: The border runs through the middle of Lake Geneva.

44030.q: Which pass takes you from Valais straight to Italy?
44030.e: The Great St Bernard links Valais with the Aosta Valley in Italy. The border is at the top of the pass.
44030.m: You can get to Italy over the Great St Bernard.

44031.q: What do you call a piece of a country that is completely surrounded by another country?
44031.e: An exclave belongs to one country but lies completely within the territory of another. One example is Büsingen.
44031.m: An exclave is surrounded by a foreign country.

44032.q: What were the officials called who guarded Switzerland's open border away from the crossings?
44032.e: Border guards also checked the border away from the crossing points. Today they are part of Swiss customs.
44032.m: Border guards watched over the border.

44033.q: Which river forms part of the border with France in the Jura?
44033.e: The Doubs flows through the Jura. Over a long stretch it separates Switzerland from France.
44033.m: The Doubs forms the border with France in the Jura.

44034.q: What is it called when people from Switzerland go shopping more cheaply in a nearby country?
44034.e: Many people cross the border to shop because lots of things are cheaper there. This is called shopping tourism.
44034.m: Shopping abroad is called shopping tourism.

44035.q: Since 2025, up to what value per person per day can you bring purchases into Switzerland without paying VAT?
44035.e: Since 1 January 2025 the duty-free allowance has been 150 francs per person per day. Before that it was 300 francs.
44035.m: The duty-free allowance is 150 francs per person per day.

44036.q: Why are you not allowed to bring ivory souvenirs into Switzerland?
44036.e: Ivory comes from elephants' tusks. To protect these animals, trading in ivory is forbidden.
44036.m: Ivory may not be imported because elephants are protected.

44037.q: What is the money called that you have to pay for some goods at the border?
44037.e: If you buy a lot abroad, you sometimes have to pay customs duty at the border. This money goes to the state.
44037.m: For some goods you pay customs duty at the border.

44038.q: In which city is the Swiss embassy in Germany?
44038.e: Embassies are usually in the capital. That is why the Swiss embassy in Germany is in Berlin, near the Federal Chancellery.
44038.m: The Swiss embassy in Germany is in Berlin.

44039.q: Which country does the ground under a foreign embassy in Bern belong to?
44039.e: The ground of an embassy remains part of the host country. However, the embassy is specially protected.
44039.m: Even under an embassy, the ground is Swiss territory.

44040.q: Which letters are on diplomats' number plates in Switzerland?
44040.e: CD stands for “Corps Diplomatique”. This is how you recognise cars belonging to embassies and diplomats.
44040.m: Diplomats' cars have the letters CD.

44041.q: Which holiday do Swiss embassies abroad celebrate with guests?
44041.e: 1 August is the Swiss National Day. Many Swiss embassies then invite guests to a celebration.

44042.q: Since 1980, which country has Switzerland represented as a protecting power in Iran?
44042.e: Since 1980 the USA and Iran have had no embassies in each other's countries. That is why Switzerland represents the USA in Iran.
44042.m: Switzerland represents the USA in Iran.

44044.q: In which city is the Swiss embassy in Italy?
44044.e: Embassies are usually in a country's capital. That is why the Swiss embassy in Italy is in Rome.
44044.m: The Swiss embassy in Italy is in Rome.

44045.q: How many embassies does a country usually have in another country?
44045.e: A country usually has only one embassy in another country. Sometimes there are also consulates in other cities.
44045.m: A country usually has just one embassy in each country.

44046.q: Which capital of a country neighbouring Switzerland has the most inhabitants?
44046.e: About 3.7 million people live in Berlin (as of 2024). That is more than in any other capital of a neighbouring country.
44046.m: Berlin is the biggest capital among the neighbouring countries.

44047.q: In which capital is the famous Ferris wheel in the Prater?
44047.e: The Ferris wheel in Vienna's Prater was built in 1897. It is one of the city's landmarks.
44047.m: The Ferris wheel in the Prater is in Vienna.

44048.e: The Spree flows right through Berlin, past the Reichstag building.

44049.q: Which capital is also a federal state of Austria in its own right?
44049.e: Vienna is a city and at the same time one of Austria's federal states.
44049.m: Vienna is both a city and a federal state.

44050.q: Which famous church in Paris burned in 2019 and reopened in 2024?
44050.e: In April 2019 the roof of Notre-Dame Cathedral burned. After being rebuilt, it reopened in December 2024.
44050.m: Notre-Dame in Paris was rebuilt after the fire.

44051.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of Berlin, just like Bern?
44051.e: Berlin's coat of arms has a black bear on it. The city of Bern also has a bear on its coat of arms.
44051.m: Berlin and Bern both have a bear on their coats of arms.

44052.q: What is the Italian word for ice cream?
44052.e: Ice cream is “gelato” in Italian. In Italy there are lots of gelaterias.
44052.m: Ice cream is gelato in Italian.

44054.q: What do you say in French when saying goodbye?
44054.e: “Au revoir” means “goodbye”. “Merci” means “thank you” and “S'il vous plaît” means “please”.
44054.m: To say goodbye in French you say “Au revoir”.

44055.q: Which train do many cross-border commuters from France take to Geneva?
44055.e: The Léman Express has run between Geneva and France since 2019. It links places such as Annemasse with the city of Geneva.
44055.m: The Léman Express links Geneva with France.

44056.q: Why do many people from neighbouring countries work in Switzerland?
44056.e: In Switzerland people usually earn more money than in the neighbouring countries. That is why many cross the border to work.
44056.m: Many cross-border commuters come because of the higher wages.

44057.q: What are cross-border commuters called in French?
44057.e: “Frontière” means “border”. That is why cross-border commuters are called “frontaliers” in French.
44057.m: Cross-border commuters are called frontaliers in French.

44058.q: Which country do most cross-border commuters working in Schaffhausen come from?
44058.e: The canton of Schaffhausen is almost completely surrounded by German territory. That is why its cross-border commuters come mainly from Germany.
44058.m: Many cross-border commuters from Germany work in Schaffhausen.

44059.q: Which two neighbouring countries does the city of Basel border?
44059.e: Basel lies on the Rhine where three countries meet. Many cross-border commuters from France and Germany work in Basel.

44060.q: Why do many cross-border commuters live abroad rather than in Geneva?
44060.e: In Geneva flats are very expensive and hard to find. In nearby France housing is usually cheaper.
44060.m: Many cross-border commuters live abroad because housing is cheaper there.

44061.q: Are cross-border commuters counted as part of Switzerland's population?
44061.e: Cross-border commuters work in Switzerland but live abroad. That is why they are not counted in Switzerland's resident population.
44061.m: Cross-border commuters are not part of Switzerland's resident population.

44062.q: Which language do cross-border commuters from France usually speak at work in Geneva?
44062.e: French is the official language in Geneva. So cross-border commuters from France can speak their own language at work.
44062.m: In Geneva people mostly work in French.

44063.q: What is the smaller, western part of Lake Constance called?
44063.e: Lake Constance is made up of the large Obersee and the smaller Untersee. Steckborn, for example, lies on the Untersee.
44063.m: The smaller part of Lake Constance is called the Untersee.

44064.q: Which German town on Lake Constance has its old town on an island?
44064.e: Lindau's old town lies on an island in Lake Constance. A causeway and a bridge link it to the mainland.
44064.m: Lindau has an old town on an island.

44065.q: Which island in Lake Constance is known for vegetables and old monasteries?
44065.e: Lots of vegetables are grown on the island of Reichenau. Its old churches are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
44065.m: Reichenau is the vegetable island in Lake Constance.

44066.q: Which old houses can you visit at Unteruhldingen on Lake Constance?
44066.e: At Unteruhldingen there are rebuilt houses standing on stilts in the water. This is how people lived by the lake thousands of years ago.
44066.m: You can visit pile dwellings on Lake Constance.

44067.q: Why is the water of Lake Constance important for millions of people?
44067.e: Lots of drinking water is taken from Lake Constance. It flows through long pipes far into southern Germany, for example to Stuttgart.
44067.m: Lake Constance supplies drinking water for millions of people.

44069.q: Which fish is caught especially often in Lake Constance?
44069.e: Whitefish is the most important food fish in Lake Constance. It is often served fried.
44069.m: In Lake Constance people mainly catch whitefish.

44070.q: According to the Federal Constitution, what applies to all authorities?
a: They may only act if the law allows it
They may do what they like
They must have every decision approved by the people
They must always obey the President of the Confederation
44070.e: Article 5 says that the law is the basis and the limit of state action. So authorities always need a rule that allows them to act.
44070.m: The state may only act on the basis of the law.

44072.q: Which legal text is at the very top of the order of law in Switzerland?
a: An ordinance of the Federal Council
44072.e: The Federal Constitution is the highest law of the country. Federal acts and ordinances must be compatible with it.
44072.m: The Federal Constitution is the highest law in Switzerland.

44073.q: Which four national languages does the Federal Constitution name?
44073.e: Article 4 of the Federal Constitution names German, French, Italian and Romansh as national languages.

44074.q: What is the Federal Constitution called in French?
44074.e: The Federal Constitution is published with equal status in the official languages. In French it is called “Constitution fédérale”, in Italian “Costituzione federale”.
44074.m: In French the Federal Constitution is called “Constitution fédérale”.

44075.q: According to Article 5 of the Federal Constitution, what must the federal government and the cantons respect besides national law?
44075.e: Article 5 paragraph 4 says: “The Confederation and the cantons shall respect international law.” This includes international treaties, for example.
44075.m: The federal government and the cantons must respect international law.

44076.q: The state must act “proportionately”. What does that mean?
a: It may not intervene more strictly than necessary
It must always spend the same amount of money
It may only act once a year
44076.e: A measure must be suitable and may not restrict more than necessary. This is stated in Article 5 of the Federal Constitution.
44076.m: Proportionate means no stricter than necessary.

44078.q: What is the majority of the cantons in a vote on the constitution called?
44078.e: In votes on the constitution, what counts besides the people is in how many cantons a majority agrees. This is called the majority of the cantons.
44078.m: In votes on the constitution, the majority of the cantons counts as well as the people.

44079.q: Which fundamental right protects the freedom of research and teaching?
44079.e: Article 20 of the Federal Constitution guarantees the freedom of academic teaching and research.
44079.m: Academic freedom protects research and teaching.

44080.q: Which fundamental right protects painters, musicians and writers in their work?
44080.e: Article 21 says: “Freedom of artistic expression is guaranteed.”

44081.q: Which treatment does the Federal Constitution expressly ban in the article on personal freedom?
44081.e: Article 10 bans torture and any other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. Prison sentences and fines, on the other hand, are allowed if a court imposes them.

44082.q: Who is first and foremost bound by fundamental rights and must respect them?
44082.e: Fundamental rights protect the individual against the state. Anyone carrying out state tasks is bound by them (Article 35).
44082.m: Fundamental rights protect people from abuses by the state.

44083.q: May fundamental rights be restricted in Switzerland?
a: Yes, but only under strict conditions
44083.e: Fundamental rights may only be restricted if a law allows it, there is a public interest and the restriction is proportionate. The core of a fundamental right always remains protected.
44083.m: Fundamental rights may only be restricted under strict conditions.

44084.q: Which fundamental right protects the right to use your own language?
44084.e: Article 18 of the Federal Constitution guarantees freedom of language. In dealings with the authorities, however, the official languages apply.
44084.m: Freedom of language protects the use of your own language.

44085.q: Which fundamental right guarantees help and care for people in need?
a: Right to assistance when in need
44085.e: Article 12 gives people in need the right to help and to the means that are essential for a life in human dignity.
44085.m: Anyone in need has the right to help.

44086.q: According to the Federal Constitution, what are court hearings and the announcement of judgements in principle?
44086.e: Article 30 paragraph 3 states that court hearings and the announcement of judgements are public. The law may provide for exceptions.
44086.m: Court hearings in Switzerland are public in principle.

44087.q: According to Article 31, what must an arrested person be told immediately?
a: The reasons for the arrest and their rights
The weather for the next day
44087.e: Anyone who is arrested must be told immediately, in a language they understand, the reasons and their rights.
44087.m: Arrested people must immediately learn the reasons and their rights.

44088.q: Which fundamental right protects the right to marry and start a family?
a: Right to marry and to have a family
44088.e: Article 14 of the Federal Constitution guarantees the right to marry and to have a family.
44088.m: The right to marry and to have a family is a fundamental right.

44089.q: Because of freedom of expression, does a private newspaper have to print every reader's letter?
a: No, freedom of expression protects against the state
44089.e: Freedom of expression forbids the state from suppressing opinions. But a private newspaper may choose for itself what it publishes.
44089.m: Freedom of expression is aimed first and foremost at the state.

44090.q: Which fundamental right allows you to inform yourself freely from generally accessible sources?
44090.e: Article 16 paragraph 3 protects the right to receive information freely and to gather it from generally accessible sources.
44090.m: Freedom of information allows you to inform yourself freely.

44091.q: Where can you turn if you think a radio or television programme breaks the law?
a: Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television
44091.e: The Independent Complaints Authority for Radio and Television (UBI) examines complaints about programmes. Before that you have to contact an ombudsman's office.
44091.m: Complaints about radio and TV programmes are examined by the UBI.

44092.q: What is it called when someone spreads defamatory claims about a person without knowing whether they are true?
44092.e: Defamation is a criminal offence. Unlike in malicious defamation, the offender does not know for certain that the claim is false.
44092.m: Even spreading unchecked claims that damage someone's honour can be a crime.

44093.q: Which statements are a criminal offence in Switzerland despite freedom of expression?
a: Calls to hatred because of religion or origin
An opinion different from the teacher's
44093.e: The criminal provision against discrimination and incitement to hatred (Article 261bis of the Criminal Code) sets limits on freedom of expression. Criticism of the authorities, on the other hand, is allowed.
44093.m: Freedom of expression ends where people call for hatred against groups.

44094.q: What is it called when someone knowingly spreads untrue things about a person to damage their reputation?
44094.e: Malicious defamation is an attack on someone's honour and a criminal offence. Freedom of expression does not protect deliberately false claims that harm others.
44094.m: Anyone who knowingly spreads lies about others commits malicious defamation.

44095.q: Besides incitement to hatred, which statement does the anti-racism criminal provision also punish?
44095.e: Article 261bis of the Criminal Code also punishes anyone who publicly denies or grossly trivialises a genocide or other crimes against humanity.
44095.m: Publicly denying a genocide is a criminal offence in Switzerland.

44096.q: What is the criminal provision called that bans calls to hatred because of origin or religion?
44096.e: The anti-racism criminal provision is in Article 261bis of the Criminal Code. The people accepted it in 1994.
44096.m: The anti-racism criminal provision protects against hatred and discrimination.

44097.q: What is a church called that is officially recognised under public law by a canton?
44097.e: In most cantons the Reformed Church and the Roman Catholic Church are recognised as established cantonal churches. For example, they may levy church taxes.
44097.m: Churches recognised by the canton are called established cantonal churches.

44098.q: Which two churches are recognised as established cantonal churches in most cantons?
a: The Reformed and the Roman Catholic
44098.e: In most cantons the Reformed and the Roman Catholic churches are established cantonal churches. In some cantons the Christian Catholic Church is also recognised.
44098.m: The Reformed and Catholic churches are usually established cantonal churches.

44099.q: What does the separation of church and state mean?
a: The state does not support any church directly
44099.e: With separation of church and state, the canton does not collect church tax for the churches and does not support them directly. Geneva and Neuchâtel have this separation.
44099.m: With separation of church and state, the state does not support any church directly.

44100.q: Why must state schools be religiously neutral?
a: Because children of all religions go to them
Because religion is banned in Switzerland
Because teachers may not have a religion
Because otherwise it would be too expensive
44100.e: Children of different religions or of no religion go to state schools. That is why the school may not favour any religion. For this reason, the Federal Supreme Court ruled in 1990 that crucifixes had to be removed from classrooms.
44100.m: State schools must be religiously neutral.

44101.q: May children simply stay away from compulsory swimming lessons for religious reasons?
a: Only if they can already swim
44101.e: Courts have decided that joint swimming lessons may be compulsory. The integration of the children is an important goal.
44101.m: Mixed swimming lessons may be compulsory.

44102.q: What does freedom of religion guarantee?
a: Everyone may freely choose their religion or have none
Everyone must belong to the same religion
The state decides each family's religion
44102.e: Freedom of religion and conscience is in the Federal Constitution. Nobody may be forced to join a religion or to stay in one.
44102.m: Everyone may choose their religion freely.

44103.q: Which religious community is also officially recognised in some cantons such as Basel-Stadt, Bern and Zurich?
44103.e: Several cantons have recognised Jewish communities under public law. Recognition is a matter for the cantons.
44103.m: In some cantons, Jewish communities are also officially recognised.

44104.q: Which ban did voters accept on 7 March 2021?
a: The ban on covering the face
44104.e: The popular initiative “Yes to a ban on full facial coverings” was accepted in 2021. Since then the ban has been in Article 10a of the Federal Constitution.
44104.m: Since 2021 a ban on face coverings has been in the Federal Constitution.

44106.q: According to the Federal Constitution, on what principle must taxes be assessed?
a: According to where the parents live
44106.e: Article 127 requires, among other things, taxation according to economic capacity. Those who have more pay more tax.

44109.q: Which law puts equality between women and men in working life into practice?
44109.e: The Gender Equality Act of 1996 bans discrimination in working life, for example in hiring or pay.
44109.m: The Gender Equality Act protects against disadvantage at work.

44110.q: Which federal law is meant to remove disadvantages for people with disabilities?
44110.e: The Disability Discrimination Act came into force in 2004. For example, it requires barrier-free access to public transport.
44110.m: The Disability Discrimination Act protects people with disabilities.

44111.q: Which fundamental right protects against arbitrary decisions by the authorities?
44111.e: Article 9 gives every person the right to be treated by state bodies without arbitrariness. Decisions must have objective reasons.

44112.q: What does equality before the law mean for a municipality that examines building applications?
a: Equal cases must be treated equally
44112.e: Equality before the law requires that equal things are treated equally and unequal things unequally. Personal relationships must play no part.
44112.m: Authorities must treat equal cases equally.

44113.q: Which question is in principle not allowed in a job interview because it can lead to discrimination?
44113.e: Under the Gender Equality Act, nobody may be disadvantaged because of a pregnancy. Asking about a pregnancy is therefore not allowed in principle.
44113.m: A pregnancy must play no part in hiring.

44114.q: What is it called when the police check people only because of their skin colour or appearance?
44114.e: Racial profiling means people are checked without any specific suspicion because of outward features. This goes against the ban on discrimination.
44114.m: Checks only because of skin colour are discriminatory.

44115.q: What does the ban on discrimination in the Federal Constitution forbid?
a: Disadvantaging people because of their origin or sex
44115.e: Nobody may be disadvantaged, for example, because of origin, sex, age, language, religion or a disability. This is in the Federal Constitution.
44115.m: Nobody may be disadvantaged because of origin, sex or disability.

44116.q: Who does the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities especially protect?
44116.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities requires states to protect people with disabilities from disadvantage. Switzerland has signed it too.
44116.m: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities protects people with disabilities.

44117.q: A landlady turns down a family only because of their skin colour. What is that called?
44117.e: Anyone who disadvantages people because of skin colour or origin is discriminating on racial grounds. Services offered to the public may not be refused for this reason.
44117.m: Disadvantage because of skin colour is racial discrimination.

44118.q: What is disadvantage called that is based only on a person's age?
44118.e: Age is one of the features that Article 8 paragraph 2 names expressly. Anyone who is disadvantaged only because of their age experiences age discrimination.
44118.m: Nobody may be disadvantaged only because of their age.

44119.q: Is it forbidden discrimination if a bus has ramps for wheelchairs?
a: No, it helps put disadvantaged people on an equal footing
Yes, it is against the constitution
Yes, because not all buses have ramps
44119.e: Measures that make up for disadvantages are allowed and welcome. The constitution even requires disadvantages for people with disabilities to be removed.
44119.m: Measures to balance out disadvantages are not discrimination.

44120.q: Which feature in the ban on discrimination protects, for example, people who live together without being married?
44120.e: Article 8 paragraph 2 bans discrimination because of a person's way of life. This includes, for example, unmarried couples living together or same-sex couples.
44120.m: Nobody may be discriminated against because of their way of life.

44121.q: Under the Data Protection Act, what may you ask a company?
a: What data it has about me
44121.e: Everyone has a right of access. They may ask what data a company is processing about them.
44121.m: You may ask what data a company has about you.

44122.q: What is the federal body called that supervises data protection in Switzerland?
a: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
44122.e: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) supervises compliance with the Data Protection Act by federal bodies and private parties.
44122.m: The FDPIC watches over data protection in Switzerland.

44124.q: Which right allows you to get your own data from a provider in a common format and take it with you?
a: Right to data release and portability
44124.e: The revised Data Protection Act gives everyone the right to ask for their data in a common electronic format or to have it transferred.
44124.m: You may take your data with you from a provider.

44125.q: What is the European Union's data protection regulation called?
44125.e: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) has applied in the EU since 25 May 2018. It also affects Swiss companies with customers in the EU.
44125.m: The GDPR is the EU's data protection law.

44126.q: May you publish a photo of a classmate on the internet without her consent?
a: No, she has a right to her own image
Yes, if the photo is funny
Yes, if you took it yourself
44126.e: Everyone has a right to their own image as part of their personal rights. In principle, recognisable photos may only be published with consent.
44126.m: You need other people's consent before publishing photos of them.

44127.q: Whose data does the Swiss Data Protection Act protect?
44127.e: Since 2023 the Data Protection Act only protects the data of people. Companies' data is no longer covered.
44127.m: The Data Protection Act protects people's data.

44128.q: What must the cantons offer for children with disabilities?
44128.e: The Federal Constitution requires the cantons to offer adequate special needs education for children with disabilities. They too have a right to education.
44128.m: Children with disabilities also have a right to schooling.

44129.q: Who is mainly responsible for schools in Switzerland?
44129.e: Article 62 of the Federal Constitution states that the cantons are responsible for the school system.
44129.m: Schools are a matter for the cantons.

44130.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who runs the Federal Institutes of Technology?
44130.e: Article 63a paragraph 1 says: “The Confederation shall operate the Federal Institutes of Technology.” The universities, on the other hand, are mostly run by the cantons.
44130.m: The ETH are run by the federal government.

44131.q: Which international agreement guarantees every child a right to education?
a: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
44131.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child of 1989 contains the right to education. Switzerland ratified it in 1997.
44131.m: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child guarantees the right to education.

44132.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who makes the rules on vocational education?
44132.e: Article 63 states that the federal government makes the rules on vocational education. That is why apprenticeships are regulated in the same way throughout Switzerland.
44132.m: The federal government makes the rules for vocational education.

44133.q: Is going to primary school voluntary in Switzerland?
44133.e: According to Article 62, primary school education is compulsory and under state management or supervision.
44133.m: Going to school is compulsory in Switzerland.

44134.q: Who mainly awards grants for education in Switzerland?
44134.e: In Switzerland, grants and education loans are mainly a matter for the cantons. The federal government contributes to them.
44134.m: Grants are mainly awarded by the cantons.

44135.q: What does the right to education belong to?
44135.e: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948 says that everyone has the right to education.
44135.m: The right to education is a human right.

44136.q: What does the guarantee of ownership protect?
44136.e: The guarantee of ownership in the Federal Constitution protects property, for example a house or a plot of land. The state may only take it away under strict conditions and with compensation.
44136.m: The guarantee of ownership protects what belongs to you.

44137.q: What is a person entitled to if the state expropriates their land for a road?
a: A seat on the municipal council
44137.e: According to Article 26, expropriations and restrictions of ownership that amount to expropriation are fully compensated.
44137.m: With an expropriation, there is full compensation.

44138.q: What is it called when the state takes away property in the public interest?
44138.e: In an expropriation, someone has to give up their property, such as land, for a public project. This requires a law and compensation.
44138.m: Expropriation is the state taking away property in return for compensation.

44139.q: Which rule often restricts the guarantee of ownership when building?
44139.e: Because of spatial planning, landowners may not build everywhere. Outside the building zones, building is heavily restricted.
44139.m: Building zones limit where you may build on your land.

44140.q: Who usually officially certifies the purchase of a plot of land in Switzerland?
44140.e: A purchase of land is only valid if it is publicly certified. This is usually done by a notary.
44140.m: Purchases of land are certified by a notary.

44141.q: Does the duty to pay taxes violate the guarantee of ownership?
44141.e: The guarantee of ownership does not protect against taxes as long as they are based on a law and do not take away all of a person's wealth.
44141.m: Taxes do not violate the guarantee of ownership.

44142.q: Which code regulates ownership, possession and the land register in Switzerland?
44142.e: The Civil Code (ZGB) of 1907 contains property law with ownership, possession and the land register.

44143.q: Where is it recorded in Switzerland who owns a plot of land?
44143.e: The land register is a public register. It shows who owns a plot of land and which rights are attached to it.
44143.m: The land register shows who owns a plot of land.

44144.q: Who monitors prices in Switzerland in areas without effective competition?
44144.e: The Price Supervisor prevents unfair prices, for example for fees, electricity or medicines. He is informally called “Monsieur Prix”.
44144.m: The Price Supervisor protects against unfair prices.

44145.q: Who basically sets shop opening hours in Switzerland?
44145.e: Shop opening hours are regulated by the cantons. That is why they are not the same in all cantons.
44145.m: The cantons decide shop opening hours.

44146.q: Which right of the cantons restricts economic freedom when selling salt?
44146.e: The salt trade is a cantonal monopoly. The cantons have given this task to Schweizer Salinen AG.
44146.m: In Switzerland, salt is a monopoly of the cantons.

44147.q: What is an organisation called that stands up for the rights of employees?
44147.e: Employees may join together in trade unions. The Federal Constitution protects this with freedom of association.
44147.m: Trade unions stand up for employees.

44148.q: May a hairdresser with a qualification from Bern also work in Zurich?
a: Yes, the qualification is valid throughout Switzerland
No, only in the canton of Bern
Only with the Federal Council's permission
44148.e: The Internal Market Act makes sure that vocational qualifications are in principle valid throughout Switzerland.
