44148.m: A Swiss vocational qualification is valid throughout Switzerland.

44152.q: Where do Swiss citizens in principle exercise their political rights?
44152.e: Article 39 paragraph 2 states that political rights are exercised at the place of residence. Anyone who moves then votes in their new municipality.
44152.m: You vote and elect where you live.

44153.q: What is the longest the cantons may make newcomers wait before they can vote on cantonal matters?
44153.e: According to Article 39 paragraph 4, cantons can set a waiting period of at most three months after a person settles there.
44153.m: The waiting period for voting after a move is at most three months.

44154.q: May Switzerland expel Swiss citizens from the country?
44154.e: Article 25 paragraph 1 states that Swiss citizens may not be expelled from Switzerland.
44154.m: Swiss citizens may not be expelled from Switzerland.

44155.q: According to the Civil Code, where is a person's place of residence?
a: Where they live intending to stay permanently
44155.e: Article 23 of the Civil Code defines the place of residence as the place where a person lives with the intention of staying permanently.
44155.m: Your place of residence is where you intend to live permanently.

44156.q: Between whom does the Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons apply?
44156.e: The Free Movement Agreement is part of the Bilateral Agreements I between Switzerland and the EU. It means that people from the EU and Switzerland can live and work in each other's territory.
44156.m: Free movement of persons applies between Switzerland and the EU.

44157.q: What is a person called who lives somewhere else during the week and returns home at the weekend?
44157.e: Weekly residents only register as weekly residents where they work or study. Their place of residence stays where they live at weekends.
44157.m: Weekly residents keep their place of residence where their family lives.

44158.q: Which obligation can restrict the freedom of residence of certain state employees?
44158.e: Municipalities or cantons can require certain employees to live near their workplace if there is a public interest, for example in the fire brigade.
44158.m: A residence requirement can restrict freedom of residence.

44159.q: Who does the freedom of residence in Article 24 of the Federal Constitution apply to?
44159.e: Article 24 is a citizen's right for Swiss nationals. For foreigners, laws and agreements such as free movement of persons apply.
44159.m: The constitution's freedom of residence applies to Swiss citizens.

44160.q: What did women's organisations submit a petition with about 250,000 signatures to the federal government for in 1929?
44160.e: In 1929 women's organisations handed the federal government a petition for women's right to vote. For a long time it had no effect, and the right to vote only came in 1971.
44160.m: As early as 1929 a large petition demanded women's right to vote.

44161.q: Is there a deadline within which signatures for a petition must be collected?
44161.e: There is no legal deadline for collecting signatures for petitions. For a popular initiative, on the other hand, the signatures must be gathered within 18 months.
44161.m: There is no deadline for collecting signatures for a petition.

44162.q: What is a person called who submits a petition?
44162.e: Anyone who submits a petition is called a petitioner.
44162.m: Anyone who submits a petition is a petitioner.

44163.q: Who first examines a petition to the Federal Assembly?
a: The President of the Confederation alone
44163.e: Petitions to parliament are assigned to a responsible committee. It can, for example, turn the petition into a parliamentary proposal.
44163.m: Petitions to parliament are first examined by a committee.

44164.q: In which part of the Federal Constitution is the right of petition?
a: In the chapter on fundamental rights
In the chapter on the army
44164.e: The right of petition is in the first chapter of the second title, among the fundamental rights (Articles 7 to 36).
44164.m: The right of petition is one of the fundamental rights.

44165.q: Who may sign a federal popular initiative, whereas a petition is open to everyone?
44165.e: Only people entitled to vote may sign a popular initiative. A petition, on the other hand, may be signed by anyone, including children.
44165.m: Only voters sign popular initiatives, but anyone can sign a petition.

44166.q: To which EU institution can EU citizens send petitions?
44166.e: Every EU citizen has the right to send a petition to the European Parliament. There a Committee on Petitions examines the submissions.
44166.m: In the EU, petitions are sent to the European Parliament.

44167.q: In what form do you submit a petition to an authority?
44167.e: A petition is a written submission to an authority. It can be submitted on paper or, today, often electronically too.
44167.m: You submit a petition in writing.

44168.q: Does an authority have to meet the demand of a petition?
a: No, it only has to take note of it
44168.e: A petition is not binding. The authority does have to take note of it, but it decides freely whether to do anything.
44168.m: A petition does not force the authority to act.

47951.q: What does the Latin word “globus” mean?
47951.e: “Globus” comes from Latin and means ball. A globe is a ball with the Earth on it.
47951.m: The word globe comes from the Latin for ball.

47952.q: How much of the Earth can you see at once when you look at a globe?
47952.e: You can never see all of a ball from one side. That is why you have to turn the globe to see the other half.
47952.m: On a globe you can only ever see about half of the Earth.

47953.q: Where is the axis of a globe fixed?
a: At the North Pole and the South Pole
47953.e: The axis goes from the North Pole through the ball to the South Pole. You can turn the globe around this axis.
47953.m: The globe turns around the axis through the two poles.

47954.q: What does a globe show better than a flat world map?
a: The true shapes of the countries
47954.e: On the ball, countries and seas are not stretched out of shape. A flat map always has to distort the round Earth a little.
47954.m: The globe shows the shapes of countries most accurately.

47955.q: Is there more water or more land on the globe?
47955.e: About two thirds of the Earth's surface is covered with water. That is why the globe is mostly blue.
47955.m: There is more water than land on Earth.

47956.q: You shine a lamp on a globe. Where on Earth is it daytime then?
a: On the side facing the lamp
47956.e: The lamp is like the sun. Where its light falls, it is day; on the other side it is night.
47956.m: It is day on the side facing the sun.

47957.q: Which continent lies around the South Pole?
47957.e: The continent of Antarctica is at the South Pole. It is almost completely covered with thick ice.
47957.m: Antarctica lies around the South Pole.

47958.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth called?
47958.e: The Pacific is the largest ocean. If you turn the globe, you see almost nothing but Pacific on one side.
47958.m: The Pacific is the largest ocean on Earth.

47959.q: How is a world map different from a globe?
a: It is round like a ball
It is shaped like a cube
It is shaped like an egg
47959.e: A world map shows the whole Earth on a flat sheet. You can fold it or hang it on the wall.
47959.m: A world map shows the round Earth on a flat sheet.

47960.e: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa. The Nile flows through the country.

47961.q: Which continents lie between the Atlantic and the Pacific on the world map?
47961.e: North and South America lie between the two largest oceans. The Atlantic is to the east, the Pacific to the west.
47961.m: North and South America lie between the Atlantic and the Pacific.

47962.q: What does a world map show that a town map does not?
47962.e: A world map shows the whole Earth with all its continents and oceans. You cannot see small things like houses on it.
47962.m: A world map shows all the continents and oceans.

47963.q: Which country is the biggest in the world and stretches from Europe to Asia?
47963.e: Russia is the biggest country on Earth by area. On the world map it stretches across the whole of northern Asia.
47963.m: Russia is the biggest country in the world.

47964.q: Why does Greenland look far too big on many world maps?
a: The round Earth is drawn flat
47964.e: When you flatten the ball, areas near the poles get stretched a lot. That is why Greenland looks huge on many maps.
47964.m: Flat world maps distort the size of countries near the poles.

47965.q: Which continent is also a single country?
47965.e: Australia is a continent and a country at the same time. It is completely surrounded by sea.
47965.m: Australia is both a continent and a country.

47966.e: Brazil is the biggest country in South America. A large part of the Amazon flows through Brazil.

47967.q: Which country is made up of islands at the far east of Asia?
47967.e: Japan lies on many islands in the Pacific, east of the Asian mainland.
47967.m: Japan is an island country in the east of Asia.

47968.q: In which part of Europe is Switzerland?
a: In the far west by the sea
47968.e: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe. It has no access to the sea.
47968.m: Switzerland is in the middle of Europe.

47969.q: How many main compass directions are there?
47969.e: The four main compass directions are north, east, south and west.
47969.m: There are four main compass directions.

47970.q: Which compass direction is opposite east?
47970.e: East and west are opposite each other, just like north and south.

47971.q: Which compass direction lies exactly between south and west?
47971.e: South-west lies between south and west. Its abbreviation is SW.
47971.m: South-west lies between south and west.

47972.q: You are facing north. Which side is east on?
47972.e: When you face north, east is on the right, west on the left and south behind you.
47972.m: If you face north, east is on your right.

47973.q: Which compass direction lies exactly between north and east?
47973.e: North-east lies between north and east. You simply put the two names together.
47973.m: North-east lies between north and east.

47974.q: What does the letter “W” stand for in compass directions?
47974.e: Compass directions are shortened to letters: N, E, S and W. The W stands for west.
47974.m: The letter W stands for west.

47975.q: Which sentence helps you remember the compass directions clockwise?
47975.e: The first letters N, E, S, W give north, east, south and west. That is the order they follow clockwise.
47975.m: Never Eat Shredded Wheat helps you remember the compass directions.

47976.q: In which direction is Italy from Switzerland?
47976.e: Italy lies south of Switzerland, beyond the Alps. Ticino borders Italy.

47977.q: How do you abbreviate the direction north-west?
47977.e: You take the first letters of north and west. North always comes first.

47978.q: In which direction is Austria from Switzerland?
47978.e: Austria borders Switzerland in the east, for example the canton of Graubünden.

47979.q: What do you need a compass for?
47979.e: A compass shows where north is. With it you can work out all the other directions.
47979.m: With a compass you find the directions.

47980.q: How do you hold a compass when reading it?
a: Upright in front of your face
47980.e: Only when the compass is lying flat can the needle turn freely. Otherwise it gets stuck.
47980.m: You must hold a compass flat.

47981.q: Why does the compass needle always point the same way?
47981.e: The needle is magnetic. The Earth is like a giant magnet and pulls the needle into a north-south direction.
47981.m: The compass needle is a small magnet.

47982.e: Magnets and iron attract the needle. Then the compass shows the wrong direction.
47982.m: Keep magnets and iron away from a compass.

47983.q: What colour is the north tip of a compass needle usually?
47983.e: On most compasses, the tip that points north is red. That way you do not mix up the ends.
47983.m: The red tip of the compass needle usually points north.

47984.q: What is the star showing the compass directions on compasses and maps called?
47984.e: The compass rose shows all the directions as a star. You find it on compasses and old maps.
47984.m: The compass rose shows all the directions.

47985.q: In which country was the compass invented?
47985.e: The first compasses were made in ancient China. Later, seafarers brought the idea to Europe.
47985.m: The compass was invented in China.

47986.q: Who especially needed a compass in the past to find the way?
47986.e: On the open sea you often cannot see any land. With a compass, seafarers could still keep their direction.
47986.m: Seafarers found their way across the sea with a compass.

47987.q: Where does the other end of the compass needle point?
47987.e: One tip points north, the other exactly the opposite way. The opposite of north is south.
47987.m: The other end of the compass needle points south.

47988.q: In which sport do you run through the forest with a map and compass?
47988.e: In orienteering you look for checkpoints in the countryside. This sport is very popular in Switzerland.
47988.m: In orienteering you need a map and compass.

a: Signatures of the people who drew it
47989.e: Map symbols stand for things such as churches, stations or forests. That way a lot fits on one map.
47989.m: Map symbols stand for things in the landscape.

47990.q: How is a river usually drawn on a map?
47990.e: Rivers and streams are blue lines on maps. The wider the river, the thicker the line often is.
47990.m: Rivers are blue lines on maps.

47991.q: On many maps, what does a small cross on a building stand for?
47991.e: A building with a cross means a church. Churches are good landmarks in a village.
47991.m: A building with a cross on a map means a church.

47992.q: What does a blue sign with a “P” show on a town map?
47992.e: The “P” stands for parking. You also see this sign on road signs.
47992.m: A P on a blue background means car park.

47993.q: What does a small tent show on a map?
47993.e: A tent stands for a campsite. You may stay overnight there in a tent or caravan.
47993.m: A tent on the map means campsite.

47994.q: What does a small aeroplane show on a map?
47994.e: The aeroplane stands for an airport or airfield. The largest airport in Switzerland is in Zurich.
47994.m: An aeroplane on the map shows an airport.

47995.q: Why are symbols used on maps instead of photos?
47995.e: There is not much space on a map. Small symbols are clear and you understand them quickly.
47995.m: Map symbols save space on the map.

47996.q: What does a bed symbol show on a map?
47996.e: A bed means that you can stay overnight there. Usually it is a hotel or some other place to stay.
47996.m: A bed on the map means somewhere to stay overnight.

47997.q: What does a small tower with battlements show on a map?
47997.e: Battlements are the notches along the top of old walls. The symbol stands for a castle or palace.
47997.m: A tower with battlements means a castle.

47998.q: What does a bus symbol show on a town map?
47998.e: The bus symbol shows where a bus stops. You can get on and off there.
47998.m: A bus on the town map shows a bus stop.

47999.q: What is the key of a map?
47999.e: The key tells you what each symbol and each colour on the map means.
47999.m: The key explains the symbols of a map.

48000.q: Where do you usually find the key?
a: At the edge of the map
In the middle of the map
48000.e: The key is usually in a corner or at the edge. That way it does not cover anything important.
48000.m: The key is usually at the edge of the map.

48001.q: What do you do if you do not know a symbol on the map?
a: Look it up in the key
Look it up on the compass
48001.e: The key explains all the symbols. There you can find out what the unknown symbol means.
48001.m: You look up unknown symbols in the key.

48002.q: Why does every map have its own key?
48002.e: Not all maps use the same symbols and colours. That is why every map explains its own symbols.
48002.m: Every map explains its symbols in its own key.

48003.q: What does the key of a hiking map explain, for example?
a: Which line is a hiking trail
What the weather will be like
Who is going on the hike
48003.e: On a hiking map, the key shows how hiking trails, huts and mountain railways are drawn.
48003.m: The key of a hiking map also explains the hiking trails.

48004.q: How easy is it to read a map without a key?
48004.e: Without a key you have to guess what the symbols mean. That is why every good map has one.
48004.m: Without a key a map is hard to read.

48005.q: In the key, a blue box has the word “lake” next to it. What is a blue area on this map, then?
48005.e: The key says that blue means a lake here. So every blue area is a lake.
48005.m: The key tells you what a colour on the map means.

48006.q: What does the key of a height map show for the colours?
a: Which colour stands for which height
48006.e: Next to each colour there is a height in metres. That way you know how high the land is at a certain place.
48006.m: The key of a height map gives each colour a height.

48007.q: What is another name for the key of a map?
48007.e: The key is also called the legend. It explains the symbols on the map.
48007.m: The key is also called the legend.

48008.q: What does NOT belong in the key of a map?
a: The symbol for a railway station
48008.e: The key only contains the symbols and colours of the map. The weather does not belong there.
48008.m: The key only contains the map's symbols and colours.

48009.q: What does the scale of a map show?
a: How much it has been made smaller
48009.e: The scale tells you how much smaller the map is than reality.
48009.m: The scale shows how much a map has been made smaller.

48010.q: How is everything on a map compared with reality?
48010.e: A whole town or country only fits on one sheet if you make everything smaller.
48010.m: On a map everything is made smaller.

48011.q: Scale 1 to 100: how long is 1 centimetre on the map in reality?
48011.e: 1 centimetre on the map is 100 centimetres in reality. 100 centimetres are 1 metre.
48011.m: At a scale of 1 to 100, 1 centimetre on the map is 1 metre in real life.

48012.q: Scale 1 to 100,000: how long is 1 centimetre on the map in reality?
48012.e: 1 centimetre times 100,000 is 100,000 centimetres. That is 1000 metres, so 1 kilometre.
48012.m: At a scale of 1 to 100,000, 1 centimetre on the map is 1 kilometre.

48013.q: What is the scale bar at the edge of a map for?
48013.e: The bar is like a small ruler. You can see which real distance matches a length on the map.
48013.m: You read off real distances with the scale bar.

48014.e: A town map is made much less small. That is why you can even see single streets and houses on it.
48014.m: The less a map is made smaller, the more details it shows.

48015.q: Scale 1 to 100: two trees are 3 centimetres apart on the map. How far apart are they in reality?
48015.e: Each centimetre on the map is 1 metre in real life. 3 times 1 metre is 3 metres.
48015.m: At a scale of 1 to 100, every centimetre becomes a metre.

48016.q: What do you see on a map that has been made much smaller?
48016.e: If you make things smaller, more land fits on the sheet. But things become smaller and less exact.
48016.m: A map that has been made much smaller shows a big area.

48017.q: What scale does a common Swiss national map for hiking have?
48017.e: The national maps of Switzerland come, for example, at a scale of 1 to 25,000. There, 1 centimetre is 250 metres.
48017.m: Many Swiss hiking maps have a scale of 1 to 25,000.

48018.q: How do you say the scale “1:50,000” out loud?
48018.e: The colon in a scale is read as “to”. 1 part on the map is 50,000 parts in reality.
48018.m: The colon in a scale is read as “to”.

48019.q: How high is the sun at the equator at midday, often?
a: Only half as high as here
48019.e: At the equator the midday sun is often almost directly overhead. Then you hardly cast a shadow.
48019.m: At the equator the midday sun is often almost straight overhead.

48020.e: The equator is the same distance from the North Pole and the South Pole everywhere.
48020.m: The equator lies halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole.

48021.q: Which large lake in Africa does the equator cross?
48021.e: The equator runs through the north of Lake Victoria. It is the largest lake in Africa.
48021.m: The equator runs through Lake Victoria.

48022.q: Roughly how long is the equator?
48022.e: The equator is about 40,000 kilometres long. That is the distance around the Earth at its widest point.
48022.m: The equator is about 40,000 kilometres long.

48023.q: Which continent does the equator run through?
48023.e: The equator goes through the middle of Africa, for example through Kenya and the Congo.
48023.m: The equator runs through the middle of Africa.

48024.q: Which country in South America is named after the equator?
48024.e: “Ecuador” is the Spanish word for equator. The line runs through this country.

48025.q: Which big river flows through South America close to the equator?
48025.e: The Amazon flows through South America just south of the equator. It carries more water than any other river.
48025.m: The Amazon flows close to the equator.

48026.q: Which kind of forest grows in many areas at the equator?
48026.e: At the equator it is warm and it rains a lot. That is why thick tropical rainforests grow there.
48026.m: Tropical rainforests grow at the equator.

48027.q: How long do day and night last at the equator?
48027.e: At the equator, day and night are almost the same length all year. Each lasts about 12 hours.
48027.m: At the equator, day and night are always about the same length.

48028.q: How does the equator run on a world map?
48028.e: On the world map the equator is a horizontal line across the middle.
48028.m: On the world map the equator is a horizontal line.

48029.e: Switzerland lies north of the equator. That is why it is in the northern hemisphere.
48029.m: Switzerland is in the northern hemisphere.

48030.q: Which line separates the northern hemisphere from the southern hemisphere?
48030.e: The equator divides the Earth into two equal halves. North of it is the northern hemisphere, south of it the southern hemisphere.
48030.m: The equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

48031.q: Where is the sun at midday in Sydney, Australia?
48031.e: Sydney is in the southern hemisphere, far south of the equator. That is why the midday sun is in the north there, not in the south as it is here.
48031.m: In the southern hemisphere the midday sun is in the north.

48032.q: Which pole is in the southern hemisphere?
48032.e: The South Pole is the southernmost point on Earth. It is in the southern hemisphere.
48032.m: The South Pole is in the southern hemisphere.

48033.q: In which hemisphere do most people live?
48033.e: There is much more land in the northern hemisphere. That is why almost nine out of ten people live there.
48033.m: Most people live in the northern hemisphere.

48034.q: Which animal lives in the wild in Australia in the southern hemisphere?
48034.e: Kangaroos live in the wild only in Australia and New Guinea. They hop on their strong back legs.

48035.q: Which animal lives in the wild in the Arctic in the northern hemisphere?
48035.e: Polar bears live in the Arctic around the North Pole. There are no polar bears at the South Pole.
48035.m: Polar bears live in the Arctic in the north.

48036.q: Which country is in the southern hemisphere?
48036.e: Argentina lies in the south of South America, far south of the equator.
48036.m: Argentina is in the southern hemisphere.

48037.q: Which continent lies entirely in the northern hemisphere?
48037.e: All of Europe lies north of the equator. Australia and Antarctica are in the south.
48037.m: Europe lies entirely in the northern hemisphere.

48038.q: What is the star called that roughly shows the direction north in the northern hemisphere?
48038.e: The Pole Star is almost exactly above the North Pole. If you look towards it, you are facing north.
48038.m: The Pole Star shows the direction north at night.

48039.q: Why do the mountains on the Swiss national map look almost real?
a: They are made of glued paper
48039.e: The national map shows the mountains with shadows, as if light were coming from the top left. That makes the landscape look three-dimensional.
48039.m: Shadows make the mountains on the map look three-dimensional.

48040.q: What does green usually show on a physical map?
48040.e: On physical maps, green shows the low areas. These are mostly plains and valleys.
48040.m: On physical maps, green shows low land.

48041.q: What does brown show on a physical map?
48041.e: The higher the land, the darker the brown. That is why the Alps are drawn in brown.
48041.m: On physical maps, brown shows the mountains.

48042.q: What does white in high mountains show on a map?
48042.e: White stands for snow and ice. That is how the glaciers in the Alps are marked.
48042.m: On maps, white shows glaciers and ice.

48043.q: On the map there is often yellow between green and brown. What does it show?
48043.e: With height, the colours go from green through yellow to brown. So yellow is in the middle.
48043.m: On physical maps, yellow shows land of medium height.

48044.q: Why is the sea dark blue in some places on maps?
48044.e: Light blue shows shallow water, dark blue deep water.
48044.m: The darker the blue, the deeper the sea.

48045.q: What do the different colours on a political map show?
48045.e: A political map shows countries and borders. Neighbouring countries have different colours so you can tell them apart easily.
48045.m: Political maps show the countries in different colours.

48046.q: What colour are forests on the Swiss national map?
48046.e: On the national map of Switzerland, forests are coloured green.
48046.m: Forests are green on the national map.

48047.q: What do you call a map that uses colours to show how high the land is?
48047.e: The physical map shows the Earth's surface with mountains, valleys and seas.
48047.m: The physical map uses colours to show the height of the land.

48048.q: What colour is Greenland usually on a physical map?
48048.e: Most of Greenland is covered with thick ice. That is why it is usually white on physical maps.
48048.m: Greenland is almost completely covered with ice.

48049.e: The Earth is a planet. It travels around the sun, just like the other planets.

48050.q: Counting from the sun, which planet number is the Earth?
48050.e: Counting from the sun, first come Mercury and Venus, then the Earth.
48050.m: The Earth is the third planet from the sun.

48051.q: How many planets travel around our sun?
48051.e: Eight planets travel around our sun. The Earth is one of them.
48051.m: Our solar system has eight planets.

48052.q: Why is the Earth also called the “Blue Planet”?
a: Because a lot of water covers it
Because the air is coloured blue
Because it is made of blue stone
48052.e: About two thirds of the Earth is covered by seas. That is why it looks blue from space.
48052.m: The Earth is called the Blue Planet because of its many seas.

48053.q: As far as we know today, what exists only on Earth?
48053.e: So far we know of no other planet where plants, animals or people live.
48053.m: Earth is the only place where we know of life.

48054.q: How long does the Earth take to travel once around the sun?
48054.e: The Earth needs about 365 days for one trip around the sun. That is one year.
48054.m: One trip of the Earth around the sun takes a year.

48055.q: Which day only happens in a leap year?
48055.e: The Earth needs a little more than 365 days to go around the sun. That is why almost every four years there is an extra day, 29 February.
48055.m: In a leap year, February has 29 days.

48056.q: Which planet is bigger than the Earth?
48056.e: Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. Mercury, Mars and Venus are smaller than the Earth.
48056.m: Jupiter is much bigger than the Earth.

48057.q: Roughly how long does it take the Earth to spin round once?
48057.e: The Earth spins round once completely in about 24 hours. That is one day with its night.
48057.m: One spin of the Earth takes about a day.

48058.q: Which side of the Earth is having daytime right now?
48058.e: Where the sun shines, it is light and day. On the side facing away, it is night.
48058.m: It is day where the sun shines.

48059.q: In which direction does the Earth spin?
48059.e: The Earth spins from west to east. Seen from the North Pole, it turns anticlockwise.
48059.m: The Earth spins towards the east.

48060.q: Around which imaginary line does the Earth spin?
48060.e: The Earth's axis is an imaginary line from the North Pole to the South Pole. The Earth spins around it every day.
48060.m: The Earth spins around its axis.

48061.q: When it is midday in Switzerland, what is it on the other side of the Earth?
48061.e: The other side of the Earth is facing away from the sun. So it is night there.
48061.m: When it is midday here, it is night on the other side of the Earth.

48062.q: Why can we not feel the Earth spinning?
a: Because we spin along with it
48062.e: We, the air and everything around us spin along evenly. That is why we do not notice it.
48062.m: We spin along with the Earth.

48063.q: What would happen if the Earth did not spin?
a: Day and night would be very long
48063.e: Without spinning, one side would have day for a very long time and the other side night for a very long time. Only the journey around the sun would slowly change that.
48063.m: If the Earth did not spin, day and night would be very long.

48064.q: How many times does the Earth spin round in a week?
48064.e: A week has seven days. The Earth spins once every day, so seven times.
48064.m: The Earth spins round once every day.

48065.q: What can you show well with a torch and a globe?
48065.e: The torch plays the sun. When you turn the globe, the bright day side moves across the countries.
48065.m: With a torch and a globe you can show day and night.

48066.q: Which is the biggest: the sun, the Earth or the moon?
a: They are all the same size
48066.e: The sun is huge. More than a million Earths would fit inside it. The moon is even much smaller than the Earth.
48066.m: The sun is much bigger than the Earth.

48067.q: What does the sun give us?
48067.e: The sun gives light and warmth. Without it, the Earth would be dark and freezing cold.
48067.m: The sun gives us light and warmth.

48068.q: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
48068.e: Light is very fast, but the way from the sun to us is long. That is why it travels for about 8 minutes.
48068.m: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us.

48069.e: Plants make their food with sunlight. Without light they turn yellow and die.

48070.q: Where does the moon get its light from?
48070.e: The moon does not shine by itself. The sun shines on it and it reflects the light.
48070.m: The moon shines in the light of the sun.

48071.q: What does the Earth travel around?
48071.e: The Earth travels once around the sun every year. All the other planets travel around it too.
48071.m: The Earth travels around the sun.

48072.q: What protects your skin from too much sun in summer?
48072.e: Sun cream protects your skin from sunburn. A hat and a T-shirt help too.

48073.q: Why does the sun look so small in the sky?
a: Because it is very far away
Because it is behind the moon
48073.e: The sun is huge, but it is about 150 million kilometres away. Things that are far away look small.
48073.m: The sun looks small because it is so far away.

48074.q: In which season do many trees lose their leaves where we live?
48074.e: In autumn the leaves of many trees turn yellow, red and brown. Then they fall to the ground.
48074.m: In autumn many trees lose their leaves.

48075.q: In which season do apple trees blossom where we live?
48075.e: In spring it gets warmer and apple trees are covered in white and pink blossom. By autumn the blossom has turned into apples.

48076.q: Around which date is the longest day of the year where we live?
48076.e: Around 21 June the sun is at its highest. Then the day is longest and summer begins.
48076.m: The longest day is around 21 June.

48077.q: Around which date is the shortest day of the year where we live?
48077.e: Around 21 December the sun is at its lowest. Then the day is shortest and winter begins.
48077.m: The shortest day is around 21 December.

48078.q: Which season is it in Australia when it is winter here?
48078.e: Australia is on the other half of the Earth. There the seasons are exactly the other way round.
48078.m: In the southern hemisphere the seasons are reversed.

48079.q: What do day and night roughly have in common around 21 March?
48079.e: Around 21 March day and night are about the same length, roughly 12 hours each. Then spring begins.
48079.m: In March and September day and night are about the same length.

48080.q: Why is it warmer in summer than in winter?
a: The sun is higher in the sky
The moon helps to warm us
48080.e: In summer the sun is high and shines for longer. Its rays then warm the ground much more.
48080.m: In summer the sun is high and warms strongly.

48081.e: The Earth's axis is tilted. On its journey around the sun, sometimes the north and sometimes the south leans more towards the sun.
48081.m: The tilted Earth's axis causes the seasons.

48082.q: When does autumn begin where we live?
48082.e: Autumn begins around 22 or 23 September. Then the days become shorter than the nights.

48083.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
48083.e: In the morning the sun appears above the horizon in the east. That is where the sky gets light first.
48083.m: The sun rises in the east.

48084.q: In which direction does the sun set?
48084.e: In the evening the sun disappears behind the horizon in the west.
48084.m: The sun sets in the west.

48085.q: Where is the sun at midday where we live?
48085.e: Seen from Switzerland, the midday sun is in the south. That is when it is highest.
48085.m: At midday the sun is in the south where we live.

48086.q: Does the sun really move across the sky?
a: Yes, it travels around the Earth
48086.e: It looks as if the sun is moving. In fact the Earth is turning away underneath it.
48086.m: The sun does not move across the sky; the Earth turns.

48087.q: When does the sun rise especially early where we live?
48087.e: In summer the sun rises before 6 o'clock. In winter it gets light much later.
48087.m: In summer the sun rises early.

48088.q: What is the beautiful red glow in the evening sky called?
48088.e: When the sun is low, the sky often turns red and orange. This is called the sunset glow.
48088.m: The red glow in the evening is called the sunset glow.

48089.q: What is the line where the sky and the Earth seem to touch called?
48089.e: The horizon is the line where the sky and the Earth seem to meet. That is where the sun rises and sets.
48089.m: The sun rises and sets on the horizon.

48090.q: Where does the sun rise earlier, in Zurich or in Geneva?
a: In both at the same time
48090.e: Zurich is further east than Geneva. So the sun rises a few minutes earlier in Zurich.
48090.m: The further east a place is, the earlier the sun rises there.

48091.q: Which way does a tree's shadow point in the morning?
48091.e: A shadow always points away from the sun. So in the morning it falls towards the west.
48091.m: A shadow always points away from the sun.

48092.q: What do we call the time when it slowly gets light in the morning?
48092.e: Shortly before the sun rises, the sky is already getting light. This is dawn.
48092.m: In the morning it gets light at dawn.

a: The sun does not rise for days
The moon shines during the day
48093.e: During the polar night the sun stays below the horizon all day. So it stays dark or twilight even at midday.
48093.m: During the polar night the sun does not rise.

48094.q: Where is there a polar night?
a: Near the North and South Poles
48094.e: The polar night only happens in the areas around the North Pole and the South Pole.
48094.m: The polar night only happens near the poles.

48095.q: In which season is there a polar night at the North Pole?
48095.e: In winter the north of the Earth is tilted away from the sun. That is why it stays dark there for a long time.
48095.m: The polar night is in winter.

48096.q: Is there a polar night in Switzerland?
48096.e: Switzerland is far away from the poles. Even in winter the sun rises here every day.
48096.m: There is no polar night in Switzerland.

48097.q: What is the line beyond which there can be a polar night?
48097.e: North of the Arctic Circle and south of the Antarctic Circle there is a polar night.
48097.m: Beyond the polar circle there is a polar night.

48098.q: Which glowing show in the sky can often be seen during the polar night?
48098.e: In the long dark nights of the far north you can often see green northern lights dancing in the sky.
48098.m: During the polar night you can often see the northern lights.

48099.q: Which animal lives in the Arctic, where there is a polar night in winter?
48099.e: Polar bears live in the far north on the sea ice. They can cope with the long, dark polar night.
48099.m: The polar bear lives in the Arctic.

48100.q: Roughly how long does the polar night last at the North Pole?
48100.e: At the North Pole the sun rises once a year and sets once a year. In between it is light or dark for about half a year.
48100.m: At the North Pole it is dark for about half a year.

48101.q: What do people need much more than usual during the polar night?
48101.e: During the polar night there is no sunlight all day. So lots of lamps are switched on in houses and on the streets.
48101.m: During the polar night you need lots of lamplight.

48102.q: Which town in Norway has a polar night in winter?
48102.e: Tromsø lies far north of the Arctic Circle. From late November to mid January the sun does not rise there.
48102.m: Tromsø has a polar night in winter.

a: The sun can be seen at midnight
The moon shines like the sun
48103.e: With the midnight sun, the sun does not set even at night. You can see it even at midnight.
48103.m: With the midnight sun, the sun does not set.

48104.q: In which season is there a midnight sun in the far north?
48104.e: In summer the north of the Earth is tilted towards the sun. Then it stays light there day and night.
48104.m: The midnight sun happens in summer.

48105.q: Which animal with large antlers lives in the far north of Europe, where there is a midnight sun?
48105.e: Reindeer live in the north of Norway, Sweden and Finland. Many of them are kept by herders there.
48105.m: Reindeer live in the far north of Europe.

48106.q: At which famous cliff in Norway do many travellers see the midnight sun?
48106.e: The North Cape is at the very top of Norway. In summer many tourists come to see the midnight sun there.
48106.m: At the North Cape you can see the midnight sun in summer.

48107.q: What is often difficult for people when there is a midnight sun?
48107.e: When it is light all night, it is hard to fall asleep. Many people hang up thick curtains.
48107.m: With the midnight sun, dark curtains help you sleep.

48108.q: Can you see the midnight sun in Switzerland?
48108.e: Switzerland is too far south. Even in summer the sun sets here every evening.
48108.m: There is no midnight sun in Switzerland.

48109.q: When is there a midnight sun at the South Pole?
48109.e: It is summer at the South Pole when it is winter here. Then the sun shines there around the clock.
48109.m: The midnight sun shines at the South Pole during our winter.

48110.q: What is the big festival around the longest day called in Sweden?
48110.e: In Sweden people celebrate Midsummer in June. Then it is light even at night in the north.
48110.m: In Sweden people celebrate Midsummer in June.

48111.q: In which area of Europe can you see the midnight sun?
48111.e: Lapland is at the very north of Finland, Sweden and Norway. There the sun does not set for weeks in summer.
48111.m: Lapland has the midnight sun in summer.

48112.q: In which direction is the midnight sun in Norway at midnight?
48112.e: At midnight the sun is on the side towards the North Pole. So in Norway you see it low in the north.
48112.m: At midnight the midnight sun is in the north.

48113.q: Why don't all countries have the same time?
a: Because it is not daytime everywhere at once
Because some countries are closer to the sun
48113.e: The Earth turns. So it is morning in one country and already evening in another. Each area has its own suitable time.
48113.m: Because the Earth turns, the whole world does not have the same time.

48114.q: What do we call an area where the same time applies everywhere?
48114.e: The Earth is divided into time zones. In one time zone everyone sets their clocks the same.
48114.m: In a time zone the same time applies.

48115.q: How many hours behind Switzerland is New York in winter?
48115.e: New York is far to the west. When it is 12 o'clock here, it is only 6 in the morning there.
48115.m: New York is 6 hours behind us.

48116.q: Which neighbouring country has the same time as Switzerland?
48116.e: Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein have the same time as Switzerland.
48116.m: Our neighbouring countries have the same time as us.

48117.q: What time is it in London when it is 10 o'clock in Bern?
48117.e: London is one hour behind Switzerland. 10 o'clock minus 1 hour makes 9 o'clock.
48117.m: London is one hour behind us.

48118.q: What do people in Switzerland do with their clocks at the end of March?
48118.e: Summer time begins at the end of March. Then you put the clock forward one hour.
48118.m: In spring you put the clock forward one hour.

48119.q: What do people in Switzerland do with their clocks at the end of October?
48119.e: Summer time ends at the end of October. Then you put the clock back one hour.
48119.m: In autumn you put the clock back one hour.

48120.q: What is the tiredness after a long flight across many time zones called?
48120.e: After a flight across many time zones, your body clock no longer matches the local time. You feel tired at the wrong time.
48120.m: Jet lag comes from flying across many time zones.

48121.q: Where in the world do people celebrate New Year first?
48121.e: The date line runs through the Pacific. Islands right next to it, such as Kiribati, are the first to start the new year.
48121.m: The first New Year celebrations happen in the Pacific.

48122.q: Which country has a great many time zones because it is so big?
48122.e: Russia stretches from Europe to the Pacific. It has eleven time zones.

48123.q: What is a small model of the Earth called?
48123.e: A globe is a small ball with all the countries and seas on it. It shows the Earth in its real shape.
48123.m: A globe is a model of the Earth.

48124.q: What do you see first when a ship comes from far away across the sea?
48124.e: Because the Earth is curved, a ship appears over the horizon from the top down. You see the mast first.
48124.m: The curve of the Earth can be seen at the horizon.

48125.q: What happens if you keep travelling straight east?
a: You come back to where you started
48125.e: Because the Earth is a ball, after one round you arrive back where you started. There is no edge.
48125.m: If you travel around the Earth, you come back to the start.

48126.q: Who led the first voyage around the world by ship?
48126.e: The voyage began in 1519 under Ferdinand Magellan. He died on the way, but one ship returned to Spain in 1522.
48126.m: The first voyage around the world began with Magellan.

48127.q: Roughly how long is the journey once around the Earth at the equator?
48127.e: The Earth's circumference at the equator is about 40,000 kilometres. That is very far.
48127.m: Once around the Earth is about 40,000 kilometres.

48128.q: What shape is the Earth's shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse?
48128.e: During a lunar eclipse the Earth's shadow falls on the moon. Its edge is always round because the Earth is a ball.
48128.m: The round shadow of the Earth shows that the Earth is a ball.

48129.q: Why don't people on the underside of the Earth fall off?
48129.e: The Earth pulls everything towards its centre. So people stand safely everywhere on the ball.
48129.m: Gravity keeps us on the Earth.

48130.q: What is at the top of a globe when it is standing normally?
48130.e: On globes and maps north is usually at the top. So the North Pole is at the top.
48130.m: On a globe the North Pole is at the top.

48131.q: Why is the axis of a globe usually tilted?
a: Because the Earth's axis is tilted too
48131.e: The real Earth's axis is tilted. The globe shows it in exactly the same way.
48131.m: The tilted axis of a globe shows the tilted Earth's axis.

a: A photo of the Earth from space
A picture taken from a plane
A photo taken from the moon
48132.e: Satellites circle high above the Earth and take pictures from above. These are called satellite images.
48132.m: Satellite images show the Earth from space.

48133.q: What does a satellite need to take pictures of the Earth?
48133.e: Satellites carry special cameras on board. They use them to photograph the Earth from above.
48133.m: Satellites take pictures of the Earth with cameras.

48134.q: What is white on satellite images?
48134.e: Clouds, snow and ice reflect a lot of light. That is why they shine white on satellite images.
48134.m: Clouds and ice are white on satellite images.

48135.q: What colour is the Sahara Desert on satellite images?
48135.e: The Sahara is a huge desert of sand and stone. From above it looks yellow to brown.
48135.m: Deserts look yellowish brown from above.

48136.q: What can you see especially well at night on satellite images of Europe?
48136.e: At night the cities shine brightly. On pictures from space you then see lots of bright dots.
48136.m: At night you can see the lights of the cities from space.

48137.q: What are weather satellites used for?
48137.e: Weather satellites show where clouds and storms are. This helps to forecast the weather better.
48137.m: Weather satellites help with weather forecasts.

48138.q: What colour are large forests on satellite images?
48138.e: Forests such as the rainforest along the Amazon look dark green from above.
48138.m: Forests are green on satellite images.

48139.q: Roughly how many times a day does the ISS space station circle the Earth?
48139.e: The ISS flies very fast and needs only about an hour and a half for one lap. So it manages a good 15 laps a day.
48139.m: The ISS circles the Earth about 15 times a day.

48140.q: Who was the first Swiss person to fly into space?
48140.e: Claude Nicollier flew into space in 1992 as the first Swiss person. Altogether he travelled four times on the Space Shuttle.
48140.m: Claude Nicollier was the first Swiss person in space.

48141.q: What can you clearly see in winter on satellite images of Switzerland?
48141.e: In winter there is a lot of snow on the Alps. So on satellite images you see a wide white band.
48141.m: In winter the Alps shine white on satellite images.

48143.q: How many continents lie entirely in the southern hemisphere?
48143.e: Australia and Antarctica lie entirely south of the equator. The other continents lie wholly or partly in the northern hemisphere.
48143.m: Australia and Antarctica lie entirely in the southern hemisphere.

48144.q: Which of these names is a continent?
48144.e: Africa is a continent. Switzerland is a country, the Mediterranean is a sea and the Alps are a mountain range.
48144.m: Africa is one of the seven continents.

48145.q: Which of these names is NOT a continent?
48145.e: Greenland is an island. It is the largest island in the world, but not a continent of its own.
48145.m: Greenland is an island, not a continent.

48147.q: Which two continents have the word ‘America’ in their name?
48147.e: North America is in the north, South America in the south. Together they are often simply called America.
48147.m: America is made up of North America and South America.

48148.q: Which continent is the second largest on Earth?
48148.e: Africa is the second largest continent on Earth. It covers about 30 million square kilometres.
48148.m: Africa is the second largest continent.

48149.q: What separates most continents from each other?
48149.e: Between the continents there are usually large oceans, for example the Atlantic or the Pacific.
48149.m: The continents are mostly separated by oceans.

48150.q: Which two continents together form a huge piece of land with no sea in between?
48150.e: Europe and Asia are joined by land. Together they are also called Eurasia.
48150.m: Europe and Asia together form Eurasia.

48151.q: Which continent is roughly four times as big as Europe?
48151.e: Asia covers about 44 million square kilometres, Europe about 10 million. So Asia is about four times as big.
48151.m: Asia is about four times as big as Europe.

48152.q: Which city is a capital in Asia?
48152.e: Beijing is the capital of China in Asia. Berlin is in Europe, Cairo in Africa and Ottawa in North America.
48152.m: Beijing is a capital in Asia.

48153.q: On which continent are China and India?
48153.e: China and India are large countries in Asia. They are among the countries with the most people.
48153.m: China and India are in Asia.

48154.q: On which continent is the highest mountain in the world?
48154.e: Mount Everest is in the Himalayas in Asia. It is about 8849 metres high.
48154.m: The highest mountain in the world is in Asia.

48155.e: Japan is made up of many islands in the east of Asia.
48155.m: Japan is an island country in Asia.

48156.q: Which ocean lies to the south of Asia?
48156.e: South of Asia, for example off India, lies the Indian Ocean.
48156.m: The Indian Ocean lies to the south of Asia.

48157.q: In which direction is Asia from Europe?
48157.e: Asia joins Europe in the east. If you travel far east from Switzerland, you reach Asia.
48157.m: Asia lies to the east of Europe.

48158.q: Which cold sea lies to the north of Asia?
48158.e: At the very north of Asia, off Siberia, lies the Arctic Ocean. It is covered in ice for much of the year.
48158.m: The Arctic Ocean lies to the north of Asia.

48159.q: Which animal lives in the wild in Asia?
48159.e: Tigers live in the wild in Asia, for example in India. Kangaroos live in Australia, llamas in South America.

48160.q: Which black and white animal lives in the wild only in Asia?
48160.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in mountain forests in China. It eats almost nothing but bamboo.
48160.m: The giant panda lives in the wild in Asia.

48161.q: Which country lies in the sea to the south-east of Australia?
48161.e: New Zealand is made up of two large islands. It lies south-east of Australia in the Pacific.
48161.m: New Zealand lies south-east of Australia.

a: It is both a continent and a country
It is at the North Pole
48162.e: Australia is a continent and a country at the same time. This is not the case for any other continent.
48162.m: Australia is both a continent and a country.

48163.q: Which animal is typical of Australia?
48163.e: The kangaroo lives in the wild only in Australia and New Guinea. It is even on Australia's coat of arms.
48163.m: The kangaroo is typical of Australia.

48164.q: What is Australia completely surrounded by?
48164.e: Australia is surrounded by sea on all sides. It does not border any other continent.
48164.m: Australia is completely surrounded by sea.

48165.q: Which famous building with roofs like sails is in Australia?
48165.e: The Sydney Opera House stands right by the harbour. Its white roofs look like sails.
48165.m: The Sydney Opera House is in Australia.

48166.q: Which ocean lies to the east of Australia?
48166.e: To the east of Australia lies the Pacific, to the west the Indian Ocean.
48166.m: The Pacific lies to the east of Australia.

48168.q: What is the inside of Australia usually like?
48168.e: In the interior of Australia there are large deserts and dry land. So most people live on the coasts.
48168.m: The interior of Australia is hot and dry.

48169.q: Which language is spoken most in Australia?
48169.e: In Australia English is the most important language.
48169.m: In Australia people mainly speak English.

48170.q: What do we call Australia together with the many islands in the Pacific?
48170.e: Australia, together with New Zealand and many islands in the Pacific, forms the region of Oceania.

48171.q: What are the first inhabitants of Australia called?
48171.e: Aboriginal people have lived in Australia for many thousands of years.
48171.m: Aboriginal people are the first inhabitants of Australia.

48172.q: What is the longest river in Europe?
48172.e: The Volga flows through Russia and is about 3500 kilometres long. No river in Europe is longer.
48172.m: The Volga is the longest river in Europe.

48173.q: Which of these countries is in Europe?
48173.e: France is a neighbouring country of Switzerland in Europe.
48173.m: Like Switzerland, France is in Europe.

48174.q: Which mountain range is in Europe and also in Switzerland?
48174.e: The Alps stretch across several countries in Europe, including Switzerland.
48174.m: The Alps are a large mountain range in Europe.

48175.q: Which sea lies between Europe and Africa?
48175.e: The Mediterranean lies to the south of Europe and the north of Africa.
48175.m: The Mediterranean separates Europe and Africa.

48176.q: Which ocean lies to the west of Europe?
48176.e: To the west of Europe lies the Atlantic. On the other side is America.
48176.m: The Atlantic lies to the west of Europe.

48177.q: Which country in Europe is the smallest country in the world?
48177.e: Vatican City lies in the middle of Rome and is the smallest country in the world.
48177.m: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.

48178.q: Which island in the north of Europe has many volcanoes and geysers?
48178.e: Iceland lies in the North Atlantic and belongs to Europe. It has many volcanoes and hot springs.
48178.m: Iceland is a volcanic island in Europe.

48179.q: Which city is a capital in Europe?
48179.e: Paris is the capital of France in Europe. Cairo is in Africa, Tokyo in Asia, Lima in South America.
48179.m: Paris is a capital in Europe.

48180.q: Which river flows from Switzerland to the North Sea?
48180.e: The Rhine rises in the Swiss Alps and flows through several European countries to the North Sea.
48180.m: The Rhine flows from Switzerland to the North Sea.

48181.q: Which money does Switzerland use, even though many countries in Europe use the euro?
48181.e: Many countries in Europe pay with the euro. But Switzerland has the Swiss franc.
48181.m: In Switzerland people pay with francs.

48182.q: In which part of Europe are Norway and Sweden?
48182.e: Norway and Sweden are at the very north of Europe. This region is also called Scandinavia.
48182.m: Norway and Sweden are in northern Europe.

48183.q: Which country is in North America?
48183.e: Canada is in the north of North America. Brazil is in South America.

48184.q: Which is the largest country in North America?
48184.e: Canada is the largest country in North America and the second largest country in the world.
48184.m: Canada is the largest country in North America.

48185.q: On which continent is the USA?
48185.e: The USA, the United States of America, is in North America.
48185.m: The USA is in North America.

48186.q: Which country lies to the south of the USA?
48186.e: Mexico borders the USA in the south. Canada is in the north.
48186.m: Mexico lies south of the USA.

48187.q: To which continent does the island of Greenland belong geographically?
48187.e: Geographically Greenland is part of North America, but politically it belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.
48187.m: Geographically Greenland is part of North America.

48188.q: Which city is in North America?
48188.e: New York is a huge city in the USA in North America.
48188.m: New York is in North America.

48189.q: Which island in the Caribbean belongs to North America?
48189.e: Cuba lies in the Caribbean Sea. Geographically the Caribbean islands count as part of North America.
48189.m: Geographically Cuba belongs to North America.

48190.q: Which country in South America is very long and narrow?
48190.e: Chile lies between the Andes and the Pacific. It is over 4000 kilometres long, but on average only about 180 kilometres wide.
48190.m: Chile is a long, narrow country in South America.

48191.q: Which long mountain range runs through South America?
48191.e: The Andes run from north to south in the west of South America. They are the longest mountain range on land.
48191.m: The Andes are South America's long mountain range.

48192.q: What are the countries from Mexico to South America often called together?
48192.e: Most people there speak languages that come from Latin. That is why we speak of Latin America.
48192.m: South America is part of Latin America.

48193.q: Which huge river flows through the rainforest in South America?
48193.e: The Amazon flows through the largest rainforest on Earth. No river in the world carries more water.
48193.m: The Amazon flows through South America's rainforest.

48194.q: Which language is spoken in most countries of South America?
48194.e: In countries such as Peru, Venezuela or Bolivia, Spanish is the main language.
48194.m: Most countries in South America speak Spanish.

48195.q: Which animal lives in the Andes in South America?
48195.e: Llamas live in the Andes. People there keep them for wool and to carry loads.
48195.m: The llama lives in the Andes of South America.

48196.q: Which city is in South America?
48196.e: Rio de Janeiro is a well-known city in Brazil in South America.
48196.m: Rio de Janeiro is in South America.

48197.q: Which ocean lies to the west of South America?
48197.e: To the west of South America lies the Pacific. To the east lies the Atlantic.
48197.m: The Pacific lies to the west of South America.

48198.q: Which slow animal hangs upside down from branches in the South American rainforest?
48198.e: The sloth lives in the trees of the rainforest in South America. It moves very slowly and usually hangs upside down.
48198.m: The sloth lives in the rainforest of South America.

48199.e: Argentina is in the south of South America, east of Chile.

48200.q: Which country is Panama's neighbour to the west?
48200.e: Costa Rica borders Panama to the west. Both countries are in Central America.
48200.m: Costa Rica is a neighbouring country of Panama.

48201.q: What do we call a narrow strip of land that connects two large landmasses?
48201.e: A land bridge is a narrow strip of land between two large areas of land. Panama is such a land bridge.

48202.q: Which country runs the Panama Canal today?
48202.e: For a long time the USA ran the canal. Since the end of 1999 it has belonged entirely to Panama.
48202.m: Today Panama runs the Panama Canal itself.

48203.q: What have people built right across Panama?
48203.e: The Panama Canal runs right across Panama. Lots of big ships pass through it every day.
48203.m: A canal for ships runs through Panama.

48204.q: Why do many ships go through the Panama Canal?
48204.e: Without the canal, ships would have to sail all the way around South America. The canal saves them many thousands of kilometres.
48204.m: The Panama Canal makes the journey for ships much shorter.

48205.q: What is the capital of Panama?
48205.e: The capital has almost the same name as the country: Panama City.
48205.m: The capital of Panama is Panama City.

48206.q: Which slow animal hangs in the trees of Panama's rainforest?
48206.e: Sloths live in the rainforests of Central and South America, including Panama. They hang upside down in the trees and move very slowly.

48207.q: Roughly what shape is Panama on the world map?
48207.e: Panama is long and narrow and lies like a curved ribbon between two oceans.
48207.m: Panama is a narrow strip of land.

48208.q: What could animals do after North and South America had joined up at Panama?
a: Walk between Asia and South America
Walk between Europe and North America
48208.e: When the land at Panama formed about three million years ago, animals could walk back and forth between North and South America.
48208.m: Animals could cross between the Americas via Panama.

48209.q: What is the narrow part of America between Mexico and South America called?
48209.e: Central America lies between Mexico and South America. Panama is its southernmost country.
48209.m: Panama is the southernmost country in Central America.

48210.q: Which language is spoken in Panama?
48210.e: Panama was a Spanish colony for a long time. That is why Spanish is the official language there.

48211.q: Roughly how many countries are there in Africa?
48211.e: There are 54 countries in Africa recognised by the United Nations. That is more than on any other continent.

48212.q: Which very long river flows in Africa?
48212.e: The Nile flows north in eastern Africa and flows into the Mediterranean. It is one of the longest rivers in the world.
48212.m: The Nile is a very long river in Africa.

48213.q: Which large desert is in the north of Africa?
48213.e: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world. It is in the north of Africa.
48213.m: The Sahara is in the north of Africa.

48214.q: In which part of Africa are Morocco and Tunisia?
48214.e: Morocco and Tunisia are in North Africa on the Mediterranean, not far from Europe.
48214.m: Morocco and Tunisia are in North Africa.

48215.e: Kenya is in the east of Africa on the Indian Ocean. Many wild animals such as lions and elephants live there.
48215.m: Kenya is a country in Africa.

48216.q: What is the narrow strait between Africa and Europe called?
48216.e: At Gibraltar, Spain and Morocco are only about 14 kilometres apart.
48216.m: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Africa and Europe.

48217.q: Which important line runs right through the middle of Africa?
48217.e: The equator divides the Earth into north and south. It runs right through the middle of Africa.

48218.q: Which continent has the most people after Asia?
48218.e: About 1.5 billion people live in Africa (as of 2024). Only Asia has more.
48218.m: Africa has the second most people.

48219.q: Which country has the most people in Africa?
48219.e: Nigeria in West Africa has about 230 million people (as of 2024), more than any other country in Africa.
48219.m: Nigeria has the most people in Africa.

48220.e: Cairo is the capital of Egypt. It is one of the largest cities in Africa.
48220.m: Cairo is a large city in Africa.

48221.e: Nobody lives permanently in Antarctica, because it is extremely cold and icy there.

48223.q: Where is most of the Earth's fresh water stored?
48223.e: About 70 per cent of the Earth's fresh water is frozen in the ice of Antarctica.
48223.m: Most of the Earth's fresh water is in the ice of Antarctica.

48224.q: How thick is the ice in Antarctica at its thickest points?
48224.e: The ice of Antarctica is almost 2 kilometres thick on average, and in some places over 4 kilometres.
48224.m: In some places the ice of Antarctica is over 4 kilometres thick.

48225.q: Which season is it in Antarctica when it is winter in Switzerland?
48225.e: Antarctica is in the southern hemisphere. There the seasons are the other way round from ours.
48225.m: When it is winter here, it is summer in Antarctica.

48226.q: Which continent is the driest on Earth?
48226.e: In the interior of Antarctica hardly any snow or rain falls. That is why it is considered the driest continent.

48227.e: A treaty from 1959 says that Antarctica may only be used peacefully and for research. It is not a country.
48227.m: Antarctica does not belong to any single country.

48228.q: Which other name is often used for Antarctica?
48228.e: The continent is called Antarctica. People often also say the Antarctic. The Arctic, on the other hand, is in the north.
48228.m: Antarctica is often also called the Antarctic.

48229.q: Is it allowed to dig for oil or metals in Antarctica?
48229.e: A treaty to protect the environment bans mining for natural resources in Antarctica.
48229.m: Mining for natural resources is forbidden in Antarctica.

48230.q: Why are there no trees in Antarctica?
48230.e: Antarctica is so cold and icy that no trees can grow.
48230.m: Antarctica is too cold for trees.

48231.q: Which continent is bigger than Europe, even though nobody lives there permanently?
48231.e: At about 14 million square kilometres, Antarctica is bigger than Europe. Yet nobody lives there permanently. Lots of people live in Africa and Asia, and Australia is smaller than Europe.

48232.q: Where on a world map can Antarctica usually be seen?
48232.e: On most world maps north is at the top. Antarctica is in the south, so it is at the very bottom.
48232.m: Antarctica is at the very bottom of the world map.

48233.q: Where is America on a European world map with Europe in the middle?
48233.e: On European maps Europe is in the middle. America is on the left, on the other side of the Atlantic.
48233.m: On our world maps America is to the left of Europe.

48234.q: Which continent is at the bottom right next to Asia on the world map?
48234.e: Australia lies south-east of Asia. So on the world map it is at the bottom right.

48235.q: Which ocean lies between Asia and America on the world map?
48235.e: The Pacific is the largest ocean on Earth. It separates Asia from America.
48235.m: The Pacific lies between Asia and America.

48236.q: Which continent is at the top left of the world map, next to Greenland?
48236.e: North America is in the north-west. So on our world maps it is at the top left.
48236.m: North America is at the top left of the world map.

48237.q: Which continent is directly below Europe on the world map?
48237.e: Africa lies south of Europe. On the world map south is at the bottom, so Africa is below it.

48238.q: Which two continents meet at Egypt?
48238.e: Egypt is in Africa, but the Sinai Peninsula already belongs to Asia. That is where the two continents meet.
48238.m: Africa and Asia meet at Egypt.

48239.q: What is a round ball with the continents shown on it called?
48239.e: A globe is a model of the Earth. It shows the continents as they lie on the ball.
48239.m: A globe is a model of the Earth.

48240.q: Which two continents are very close together on the world map, separated only by the narrow Bering Strait?
48240.e: In the far north only the narrow Bering Strait separates Asia from North America.
48240.m: The Bering Strait separates Asia and North America.

48241.q: Which continent is to the left of Africa on the world map, on the other side of the Atlantic?
48241.e: To the west of Africa lies the Atlantic. On the other side is South America.
48241.m: South America lies to the west of Africa.

48242.q: On which ocean is the city of Los Angeles in the USA?
48242.e: Los Angeles is on the west coast of the USA. That is where the Pacific begins.
48242.m: Los Angeles is on the Pacific.

48243.e: A sailor had calm weather on his voyage across this ocean. So he named it ‘Mar Pacífico’, the peaceful sea.

48244.q: Which big city in Canada is on the Pacific?
48244.e: Vancouver is on the west coast of Canada. Toronto, Montreal and Ottawa are far to the east of the country.
48244.m: Vancouver is a port city on the Pacific.

48245.q: What is the group of islands in the Pacific that includes Tahiti, for example, called?
48245.e: Polynesia is made up of over a thousand islands in the middle of the Pacific. They include Tahiti, Samoa and Tonga.

48246.q: Which island country, known for the kiwi bird, is in the Pacific?
48246.e: New Zealand is in the south-west of the Pacific. The kiwi is a bird that cannot fly and is the country's national animal.
48246.m: New Zealand is an island country in the Pacific.

48247.q: Which ocean is the deepest in the world?
48247.e: The deepest points of all the seas are in the Pacific. In some places it goes down more than 10 kilometres.
48247.m: The Pacific is the deepest ocean.

48248.q: Which US state borders both the Pacific and the Arctic Ocean?
48248.e: Alaska is in the far north-west of North America. In the south it borders the Pacific, in the north the Arctic Ocean.
48248.m: Alaska is on the Pacific and the Arctic Ocean.

48249.q: Which country in South America is on the Pacific?
48249.e: Peru is on the west coast of South America, on the Pacific. Brazil and Uruguay are on the Atlantic, and Paraguay has no sea.

48250.q: Which is bigger: the Pacific or all the land on Earth put together?
48250.e: The Pacific covers about 165 million square kilometres. All the land on Earth put together is smaller.
48250.m: The Pacific is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

48251.q: What is the Great Barrier Reef off Australia?
48251.e: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the east coast of Australia. It is the largest coral reef on Earth.
48251.m: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world.

48252.q: Which country in Europe has a long coast on the Atlantic?
48252.e: Portugal is at the far west of Europe. Its whole coast is on the Atlantic.

48253.q: Which giant from the Greek myths is the Atlantic named after?
48253.e: In the Greek myths the giant Atlas carries the sky on his shoulders. The Atlantic was named after him.
48253.m: The Atlantic gets its name from the giant Atlas.

48254.q: Which sea did Charles Lindbergh fly across in 1927, as the first person to do so alone and without stopping?
48254.e: In 1927 Charles Lindbergh flew from New York to Paris in about 33 hours. He was all alone in the plane.
48254.m: In 1927 Lindbergh flew alone across the Atlantic.

48255.q: Which big US city is on the Atlantic?
48255.e: New York is on the east coast of the USA, on the Atlantic. Los Angeles, San Francisco and Seattle are on the west coast.
48255.m: New York is on the east coast, on the Atlantic.

48256.q: Which group of Spanish islands lies in the Atlantic off Africa?
48256.e: The Canary Islands lie off the coast of Morocco in the Atlantic. The Balearic Islands, by contrast, are in the Mediterranean.
48256.m: The Canary Islands are in the Atlantic.

48257.q: Which country in southern Africa is on the Atlantic?
48257.e: Namibia is on the west coast of southern Africa. Kenya is on the Indian Ocean, and Ethiopia and Zambia have no sea at all.

48258.q: Which warm ocean current flows through the Atlantic to Europe?
48258.e: The Gulf Stream brings warm water from near America all the way to Europe. That is why winters in Western Europe are milder. The Labrador Current and the Humboldt Current are cold.
48258.m: The Gulf Stream brings warm water to Europe.

48259.q: Which island with many volcanoes lies in the North Atlantic?
48259.e: Iceland lies in the north of the Atlantic. It has many volcanoes, geysers and hot springs.
48259.m: Iceland is a volcanic island in the North Atlantic.

48260.q: The Rhine from Switzerland flows into the North Sea. Which ocean does the North Sea belong to?
48260.e: The North Sea is a marginal sea of the Atlantic. So water from the Swiss Alps reaches the Atlantic via the Rhine.
48260.m: The North Sea belongs to the Atlantic.

48261.q: Which country with thousands of islands lies between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific?
48261.e: Indonesia is made up of over 17,000 islands. In the south and west it borders the Indian Ocean, in the east the Pacific.

48262.q: Which country is the Indian Ocean named after?
48262.e: The ocean lies to the south of India. That is why it bears the name of this country.
48262.m: The Indian Ocean is named after India.

48263.q: Which is the third largest ocean in the world?
48263.e: The Indian Ocean is smaller than the Pacific and the Atlantic, but bigger than the two polar oceans.
48263.m: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean.

48264.q: Which island country in the Indian Ocean is known for giant tortoises?
48264.e: The Seychelles lie in the Indian Ocean north of Madagascar. Very large land tortoises live on their islands.
48264.m: Giant tortoises live on the Seychelles.

48265.q: On which island in the Indian Ocean did the dodo bird once live?
48265.e: The dodo was a large bird that could not fly. It lived only on Mauritius and has been extinct for over 300 years.
48265.m: The dodo once lived on Mauritius.

48266.q: Which island country lies in the Indian Ocean south of India?
48266.e: Sri Lanka lies just south of the tip of India. The island is known for its tea.
48266.m: Sri Lanka is an island south of India.

48267.q: Which ocean is considered the warmest in the world?
48267.e: Most of the Indian Ocean lies in warm regions near the equator. That is why its water is the warmest on average.
48267.m: The Indian Ocean is the warmest ocean.

48268.q: Which continent lies to the east of the Indian Ocean?
48268.e: To the west of the Indian Ocean lies Africa, to the east Australia. The city of Perth is on its coast.
48268.m: Australia lies to the east of the Indian Ocean.

48269.q: Which island off East Africa in the Indian Ocean is known as the ‘Spice Island’?
48269.e: Spices such as cloves have been grown on Zanzibar for a long time. The island belongs to Tanzania.
48269.m: Zanzibar is a spice island in the Indian Ocean.

48270.q: Which bird flies from the Arctic to Antarctica and back again every year?
48270.e: The Arctic tern breeds in the far north and flies to Antarctica in winter. No other animal migrates so far every year.
48270.m: The Arctic tern flies from pole to pole.

48271.q: Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
48271.e: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and also the shallowest of the five oceans.
48271.m: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean.

48272.q: What covers a large part of the Arctic Ocean?
48272.e: Because it is very cold there, the sea water freezes. A thick layer of ice then floats on the sea.
48272.m: Lots of ice floats on the Arctic Ocean.

48273.q: What is a strong ship that forces its way through the ice of the Arctic Ocean called?
48273.e: An icebreaker has a very strong hull. It drives up onto the ice and breaks it with its weight.
48273.m: An icebreaker clears a path through the ice.

48274.q: Which country has the longest coast on the Arctic Ocean?
48274.e: Russia is the largest country on Earth. Its whole north coast is on the Arctic Ocean.
48274.m: Russia has the longest coast on the Arctic Ocean.

48275.q: Which whale of the Arctic Ocean can live to over 200 years old?
48275.e: The bowhead whale lives in the cold seas of the Arctic. Researchers have found animals that were over 200 years old.
48275.m: The bowhead whale can live to a great age.

48276.q: Which bird with a colourful beak breeds on coasts in the far north?
48276.e: The puffin has a colourful beak like a parrot. It breeds on rocky coasts in the north and dives for small fish.
48276.m: The puffin has a colourful beak.

48277.q: What do people like to build on the beach out of wet sand?
48277.e: Wet sand sticks together well. So you can build castles with towers and walls out of it.
48277.m: You build sandcastles out of wet sand.

48278.q: Which completely white whale lives in the Arctic Ocean?
48278.e: The beluga is also called the white whale. It lives in cold seas around the North Pole.
48278.m: The beluga is a white whale of the Arctic.

48279.q: Which ocean lies all around Antarctica?
48279.e: The Southern Ocean completely surrounds the continent of Antarctica at the South Pole.
48279.m: The Southern Ocean lies all around Antarctica.

48280.q: Which whale with very long flippers eats krill in the Southern Ocean in summer?
48280.e: In summer humpback whales travel to the cold seas around Antarctica. There they eat huge amounts of krill.
48280.m: Humpback whales eat krill in the Southern Ocean.

48281.q: Which small crustaceans are an important food for many animals in the Southern Ocean?
48281.e: Krill are tiny crustaceans that live in huge swarms. Whales, seals and penguins eat them.
48281.m: Krill is food for many sea animals.

48282.q: Which animal is the largest animal in the world and also lives in the Southern Ocean?
48282.e: The blue whale can grow to about 30 metres long. It is the largest animal that has ever lived.
48282.m: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

48283.q: What are the large icebergs in the Southern Ocean made of?
48283.e: Icebergs break off from the glaciers and ice sheets of Antarctica. They are made of frozen water and float in the sea.
48283.m: Icebergs are pieces broken off glaciers.

48284.q: What is the stormy sea between South America and Antarctica called?
48284.e: The Drake Passage lies between the southern tip of South America and Antarctica. There are often huge waves and strong storms there.
48284.m: The Drake Passage is a very stormy sea.

48285.q: What is the water like in the Southern Ocean?
48285.e: It is cold all year round around Antarctica. The water is often only just above freezing point.
48285.m: The water in the Southern Ocean is ice cold.

48286.q: Which fish in the icy Southern Ocean have a kind of antifreeze in their blood?
48286.e: Icefish live in the sea around Antarctica. Special substances in their bodies stop them from freezing in the icy water.
48286.m: Icefish have a kind of antifreeze in their blood.

48287.q: Which seabird with huge wings glides over the Southern Ocean?
48287.e: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of all birds, about 3 metres. It can glide over the sea for hours without flapping its wings.
48287.m: The albatross glides over the Southern Ocean.

48288.q: Which sea in Europe contains only a little salt?
48288.e: Many rivers with fresh water flow into the Baltic Sea. That is why it is much less salty than other seas.
48288.m: The Baltic Sea is only slightly salty.

48289.q: Roughly how much salt is in one litre of sea water?
48289.e: Sea water contains about 3.5 per cent salt on average. That is about 35 grams in one litre, or roughly seven teaspoons.
48289.m: One litre of sea water contains about 35 grams of salt.

48290.q: What is left behind when sea water evaporates in the sun?
48290.e: When it evaporates, only the water goes into the air. The salt stays behind.
48290.m: When sea water evaporates, salt is left behind.

48291.q: What is a place where salt is obtained from sea water called?
48291.e: At a saltworks, sea water is left to evaporate in shallow pools. Then the salt can be collected.
48291.m: Salt is obtained at a saltworks.

48292.q: Where does the salt in the sea come from?
48292.e: Rain dissolves tiny amounts of salt out of rocks. Rivers carry it into the sea, where it stays for a very long time.
48292.m: Rivers carry salt from rocks into the sea.

48293.q: Roughly how much of the Earth's surface is covered by sea?
48293.e: About 71 per cent of the Earth's surface is sea. That is why the Earth is also called the blue planet.
48293.m: Most of the Earth is covered by sea.

48294.q: What do we call water from lakes and rivers that is hardly salty?
48294.e: The water in Swiss lakes such as Lake Zurich or Lake Geneva is fresh water. It contains only very little salt.
48294.m: Lakes in Switzerland have fresh water.

48295.q: At roughly what temperature does sea water freeze?
48295.e: Salt in the water means it only freezes at a lower temperature. Sea water freezes at about minus 2 degrees Celsius.
48295.m: Sea water only freezes below zero degrees.

48296.q: Roughly how much of the water on Earth is salt water?
48296.e: Almost all the water on Earth is salty sea water. Only about 3 per cent is fresh water.
48296.m: Almost all the Earth's water is salty.
